# Focus-app (Monolith) — Audit Round 5: Comparative Audit vs the Focus-App Market

Scope: what Monolith is missing, where it loses head-to-head against shipping rival focus apps, and how its design compares — features, positioning, craft and execution. Defect findings from rounds 1–3b (684) were excluded; every finding here is new territory: an absence, a comparative loss, or a design verdict, each checked against what a named rival actually ships and against Monolith's real code.

Findings about store presence, listing assets, search discoverability and the absence of monetisation were removed from this report: the app is not published, so those are not product findings. Findings where Monolith out-builds a rival are included alongside the losses (the wins were briefly removed under a losses-only filter, then restored on Sarthak's instruction — 'keep the wins').

**Totals: 1104 findings — 253 critical, 595 high, 255 medium, 1 low (main report 830; APK supplements: Blockit 43, Forest 25, ScreenZen 25, StayFree 28, AppBlock 22, Opal 22, one sec 22, YPT 23, Zario 23, Flipd 24, Freedom 17).** Grand total across all rounds: 1788.

Dedup: 0 exact-title repeats vs the 684 prior findings, and a title-similarity sweep against all 684 prior titles found no substantive repeats in the final set.

Head-to-head supplements from static reverse engineering of the rivals' actual APKs (Blockit, Forest, ScreenZen, StayFree, AppBlock, Opal, one sec, YPT, Zario, Flipd, Freedom) are appended at the end of this report. Foqos has no Android APK (iOS-only), so it has no supplement.

## The worst new charges

1. **[New territory] Proof-of-focus is unverifiable by anyone else: signed sessions exist but no shareable, externally verifiable credential is ever issued**
2. **[New territory] No physical key exists: NFC-tag arming/disarming is a proven category primitive and Monolith has literally zero NFC code**
3. **[New territory] No progressive-overload plan: every session is an isolated manual guess, capacity never builds by design**
4. **[New territory] No wind-down descent: SLEEP is an instant cliff-edge lockdown with no taper, grayscale/dim phase, pre-bed ramp or charging trigger**
5. **[New territory] No stake escrow: quitting costs nothing real, while Forfeit/stickK/Beeminder put actual money in forfeit on a verified miss**
6. **[New territory] No AI adjudicator at the gate: every peek, break and emergency is a dumb fixed tariff while rivals ship negotiating AI**
7. **[New territory] No calendar integration at all: routines are blind weekly clock windows while the user's real life lives in a calendar Monolith never reads**

11. **[Unrealised potential] No session soundscape exists: the engine is architecturally forbidden from making any sound longer than 160ms**
12. **[Unrealised potential] Progression is exhausted in under a week: six curios total and a 70-brick tower ceiling, with no seasons, tiers or expansion**

15. **[Unrealised potential] The tactile language vanishes at the intercept: the Airlock is a passive countdown and two tap chips, not a sled ritual**
16. **[Unrealised potential] No free-text journal exists: a 'day' can hold exactly one of three preset words and not a single sentence the user wrote**

20. **[Unrealised potential] The 'desk clock' never shows the time of day — its only numeral is a session countdown**
21. **[Unrealised potential] The seal is unwitnessed and unshareable: the signature ritual produces no artifact anyone else can ever see**
22. **[Head-to-head losses] No friction outside an armed session: one sec guards every open, Monolith guards only pre-planned hours**
23. **[Head-to-head losses] One passive numeral vs one sec's per-app intervention library: no guided breath, no active task, no adjustable or escalating length**
24. **[Head-to-head losses] No always-on protection: every ScreenZen control works 24/7, Monolith blocks nothing unless a session was armed in advance**

26. **[Head-to-head losses] No growing thing to lose: session is a progress bar, not Forest's living tree that grows, withers and accumulates into a forest**
27. **[Head-to-head losses] No desktop client whatsoever: the laptop — the primary distraction surface — is completely unblocked**
28. **[Head-to-head losses] No Focus Score: no real-time single verdict on the day, no focused-vs-distracted split**
29. **[Head-to-head losses] No weekly Focus Report: no evolution, no time-saved vs baseline, no peer benchmark**
30. **[Head-to-head losses] No Strict Mode: no standalone lock that freezes rules, schedules and uninstall behind a chosen unlock condition**
31. **[Head-to-head losses] No usage-insight product at all: built-ins show you your whole phone, Monolith only measures itself**
32. **[Head-to-head losses] No human accountability at all: no body-doubling, study groups, friends or rankings that rivals' 5-star reviews credit for making them show up**
33. **[Improvement backlog] P0 backlog: no cross-device sync or desktop/browser companion — blocking stops at the phone while distraction moves to the laptop**
34. **[Improvement backlog] P0 backlog: no usage analytics or insights surface — no weekly/monthly trends, per-app history, pickups or focus score, only today's minutes**
35. **[Improvement backlog] P1 — No personal baseline: no quiz, no usage report, no goal — the data is collected and never shown to the user**
36. **[Improvement backlog] P1 — No daily focus goal: the day has no target, so day 1 ends with nothing to return for**
37. **[Improvement backlog] P2 — Zero re-engagement notifications: once a user stops opening the app, Monolith never contacts them again**

## Findings by subject

### New territory — 40 findings (10 critical, 20 high, 10 medium, 0 low)

_Monolith perfected the sealed room but built nothing beyond its walls — no verifiable proof to show the world, no forecast of the next urge, no training to survive without the app, and no earned economy inside it — leaving four category-first territories wide open while fringe rivals colonise one of them already._

#### [CRITICAL] Proof-of-focus is unverifiable by anyone else: signed sessions exist but no shareable, externally verifiable credential is ever issued

No benchmark ships a tamper-evident focus credential: Forest and Focus Flip 'share your session results' as screenshots/stats images, StayFree's ceiling is a CSV export of usage data, and Focusmate's only proof is a human partner watching on video — all forgeable in seconds. Monolith is sitting on the category's only signing machinery and wastes it on self-interrogation: CryptoIntegrityManager.kt:53 signSessionState HMAC-signs every session, but verifySessionState (CryptoIntegrityManager.kt:83) only re-checks the signature on the same device, and ReceiptSheet.kt:56-80 offers exactly one action — dismiss. There is no ACTION_SEND, export, QR or verification path anywhere in the codebase. A student who sealed 3 hours for a teacher, tutor or parent can produce nothing more credible than a screenshot, so the seal ritual's entire evidentiary value evaporates the moment anyone else needs to believe it. A signed, offline-verifiable proof-of-focus receipt (payload + signature + public verification page/key) is unclaimed territory that fits the seal-and-receipt identity exactly.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/CryptoIntegrityManager.kt:53,83; app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:56`

#### [CRITICAL] No physical key exists: NFC-tag arming/disarming is a proven category primitive and Monolith has literally zero NFC code

Benchmark: Brick built an entire company on a $59 NFC puck — tap phone to Brick to arm the block, and the ONLY way to disarm is to physically walk back to the puck and tap again; it also ships 5 emergency unbricks (Fast Company; banthebots.org blocker comparison). Free Android rivals ship the same primitive with commodity tags: TapBlok (open source) writes a token to any NDEF tag to start/stop sessions, OFFTIME and Foqos arm via NFC tag or QR code placed out of reach. Monolith's state: zero — `grep -ri nfc` across all .kt/.xml/.kts returns nothing, and AndroidManifest.xml:6-14 declares no NFC permission and no <uses-feature android.hardware.nfc>. Every arm and every exit in Monolith is an on-screen tap in the same hand holding the phone, so its entire commitment model collapses to willpower at the exact moment willpower is scarcest; a 20-cent NTAG sticker on the desk would give it the one thing no software flow can fake: distance.

Location: `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:6-14`

#### [CRITICAL] No progressive-overload plan: every session is an isolated manual guess, capacity never builds by design

Fitbod autoregulates session-to-session — raising load/reps when a set feels easy and backing off when it is a grind — and Alpha Progression adds planned deload weeks and RIR-based progression; Nike Training Club ships multi-week programs. No focus rival in the set ships this either, which is the opening. Monolith has no plan object at all: RoutineEntity (MonolithModels.kt:550-571) is only name/startMinutes/endMinutes/daysMask/loadoutName/enabled/pausedUntilMillis/scheduleEditedAtMillis — no target progression, cycle week, step rule or deload. startSession (MonolithRepository.kt:1321-1365) takes a caller-supplied durationMinutes every time and writes it verbatim as targetDurationSeconds. History is computed and then discarded as prescription: compute7DayHistory (MonolithRepository.kt:2361-2405) only sums totalMinutes/blocks25mCount/interceptionsCount per day; no code reads it to set tomorrow's dial, block count or strictness. A user who nails 25 min for two weeks and a user who fails 90 min daily get the identical blank dial.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:550`

#### [CRITICAL] No wind-down descent: SLEEP is an instant cliff-edge lockdown with no taper, grayscale/dim phase, pre-bed ramp or charging trigger

Google Digital Wellbeing Bedtime mode is a staged descent, not a switch: schedule-or-while-charging activation, grayscale, dimmed wallpaper, dark theme, keep-screen-dark and DND layered together; Headspace sells an explicit 'Wind downs' step before sleep. Monolith's entire night is one binary edge: RoutineEntity carries only startMinutes/endMinutes/loadoutName (MonolithModels.kt:550-570), the seeded SLEEP routine jumps straight to full lockdown at 20:00 (MonolithRepository.kt:849-851), and SmartLoadout.SLEEP is defined purely as a block list — 'Blocks every distracting app except Phone, Clock, and Maps' (MonolithModels.kt:54-58). A grep for grayscale/dim/brightness/charging across app/src/main/java returns zero hits: no 60/30/10-minute pre-bed reminder ramp, no visual de-stimulation phase, no plug-in-to-charge trigger, no progressively tightening tier. At 19:59 the phone is fully stimulating; at 20:00 it is a brick — the exact cliff sleep rituals exist to remove.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:54-58,550-570; app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithRepository.kt:849-851`

#### [CRITICAL] No stake escrow: quitting costs nothing real, while Forfeit/stickK/Beeminder put actual money in forfeit on a verified miss

Forfeit charges the card amount the user chose when verified evidence of a commitment never arrives, stickK forfeits a named pledge to a recipient set in a signed commitment contract, and Beeminder charges an escalating real-money pledge the moment tracked data falls off the committed path — all three sell the one thing Monolith cannot offer: failure that costs something. Monolith's only 'spend' ledger is EmergencyBreakSpendEntity (app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:442-449), which records heldSeconds of a free, weekly-refilling token; the full entity list (focus_tasks, blocked_apps, focus_profiles, focus_sessions, emergency_break_spends, intercept_logs, captured_notifications, blocked_sites, routines, guard_settings, day_notes at MonolithModels.kt:100-793) contains no stake, deposit, escrow, payment or beneficiary field anywhere. The bitter irony: Monolith already built the adjudication machinery a stake product needs — HMAC-signed receipts and ELAPSED_CLEAN/MISSED verdicts — and spends it on forging a text curio (FocusSessionEntity.forgedArtifactId, MonolithModels.kt:267-300). A user whose willpower problem is severe enough to need real loss has no reason to pick this app over Forfeit.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:442-449`

#### [CRITICAL] No AI adjudicator at the gate: every peek, break and emergency is a dumb fixed tariff while rivals ship negotiating AI

Zario ships Smart Coaching: an AI the user negotiates with for extra screen time, which grants or denies access to distracting apps — adjudication, not a tariff. Monolith has no adjudicator at all: every escape is a fixed constant (PEEK_DURATION_SECONDS lease, one weekly emergency token, 60s valve hold — AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:665-678), regardless of the stated reason, the session's declared task, or the user's history. The capability is real and on-device in 2026 (Gemini Nano via ML Kit GenAI Prompt API through AICore, no weights in the APK), yet the only AI dependency in the project sits unused: libs.versions.toml:80 defines firebase-ai and app/build.gradle.kts:105 leaves it commented out; there is no ML Kit, LiteRT or Prompt API anywhere in the tree. A Nano judge that reads the typed reason against the sealed intention and past deflections, then grants a scoped, single-purpose opening (this conversation, this OTP, this map) instead of a blanket 2-minute package lease, is unclaimed territory in this category and a direct fit for the Airlock ritual.

Location: `app/build.gradle.kts:105; app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:665`

#### [CRITICAL] No calendar integration at all: routines are blind weekly clock windows while the user's real life lives in a calendar Monolith never reads

Benchmarks: Opal ships calendar-synced working hours/routines that block apps automatically plus Focus Mode sync (App Store listing); Google/Android Focus and DND activate from calendar events, and Apple Focus turns on for calendar events. Monolith: AndroidManifest.xml declares no READ_CALENDAR (0 matches alongside 0 ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION/ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION), and its only scheduling primitive, RoutineEntity at app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:550-570, stores nothing but startMinutes, endMinutes, daysMask and a loadout name - no event id, no calendar source, no holiday/exception field. The user must hand-maintain a second, fake calendar inside the app; the day their class moves, a holiday lands, or a shift swaps, Monolith either judges a phantom window MISSED or leaves the real commitment completely unprotected.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:550`

#### [CRITICAL] No physical key exists: no NFC tag or printed QR can seal or release a session, so the lock and its key are the same pocketable screen

Brick ($59 NFC puck: tap to brick, tap again — after physically returning to wherever it was left — to unbrick, 5 emergency unbricks total) and Unpluq (NFC keyfob Tag unlock) prove the category's hardest users pay for physical separation; free Foqos/TapBlok do the same with any NFC sticker or a printed QR code, so no hardware business is required. Monolith has zero physical key: AndroidManifest.xml:6-12 declares no NFC permission or <uses-feature android.hardware.nfc>, MainActivity has no NFC intent-filter, and a codebase-wide search returns 0 hits for NfcAdapter/SensorManager/Geofence — every exit (peek, 60s emergency-valve hold) is an on-screen gesture on the same device being escaped from, so the unlock always travels in the user's pocket.

Location: `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:6-12`

#### [CRITICAL] Desk clock never becomes a room object on its own: no DreamService, no charging/dock/landscape auto-activation — only a manual mid-session tap

Benchmark: Apple StandBy (iOS 17+) has no launch button — it auto-activates when the phone is charging and propped in landscape, turning it into a bedside/desk smart display; Android's own DreamService API exists precisely for this, launching an app's lean-back screensaver when a charging device is idle or docked, and Google Clock ships a screensaver on that trigger. Monolith: zero DreamService, zero POWER_CONNECTED/dock receiver and zero charging trigger anywhere — AndroidManifest.xml declares only Shield/Accessibility/NotificationListener services and no dream service, and the clock's sole entry point is a manual in-session tap, TactileDeckScreen.kt:907-911 ('DESK CLOCK' chip, rendered only while a session runs) wired to MainActivity.kt:743-750's in-app overlay. A room object you must unlock, navigate and tap into existence — mid-session only — is a screen, not furniture.

Location: `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:40-140; app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:907`

#### [CRITICAL] A timestamped urge time-series is logged forever and aggregated into exactly one number — no temptation pattern, danger hour, or predictive guard exists

Opal turns block/usage events into a daily Focus Score and a weekly Focus Report that shows how screen time evolved and surfaces usage patterns (opalapp.com program page; App Store listing). Monolith records a strictly richer event than Opal ever sees — every reach is logged with timestamp, package, the session's stated intention, outcome and trigger reason in intercept_logs (MonolithModels.kt:451-460, written at MonolithRepository.kt:2104-2121) — yet the only aggregation any surface performs is one lifetime integer, totalInterceptions (MonolithViewModel.kt:526-527). No per-app temptation ranking, no danger-hour pattern, no per-intention survival rate, no forecast or pre-emptive guard suggestion is ever computed from the table; the per-app interceptCount (MonolithModels.kt:240) is spent entirely as a catalogue sort key (MonolithDao.kt:13). The app sits on a personal relapse dataset no rival can match and reads a single sum from it.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:451-460; app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/MonolithViewModel.kt:526-527`

#### [HIGH] No urge forecast: Monolith logs every temptation with timestamp and trigger, then never predicts the next one or pre-arms against it

Every benchmark's intelligence faces backwards: Opal sells retrospective Focus Scores and session reports, StayFree offers after-the-fact usage insights and CSV export — none predicts a user's personal high-risk window and pre-arms blocking before the urge arrives. Monolith already collects the exact training data and does nothing forward-looking with it: InterceptLogEntity (MonolithModels.kt:451) records timestamp, package, intention, outcome and trigger reason for every deflection, inserted at MonolithRepository.kt:2112 and :2347 and range-queryable via MonolithDao.kt:324, yet the codebase contains zero prediction/forecast code and gradle/libs.versions.toml carries no inference library of any kind. Routines stay dumb fixed clock windows while the user's own relapse pattern — e.g. Shorts at 23:40 after missed sessions — sits in an append-only log. An on-device urge forecast that warns at 23:15 and offers a pre-emptive seal is shipped by no focus app in the benchmark set.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:451; app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithRepository.kt:2112`

#### [HIGH] Blocking without training: no temptation-rehearsal mode turns intercepts into graded resistance practice

The benchmark set only reacts at the moment of failure: one sec inserts a breathing pause before an app opens, Opal shows pause/delay screens when an urge strikes mid-session, ScreenZen adds friction delays — none runs scheduled, graded temptation practice between sessions, and the urge-surfing/CBT tooling that does exist lives in addiction-recovery apps (Delust, QUITTR) that are not blockers and never rehearse against the user's real blocked apps under a real seal. Monolith's entire 'training' surface is four canned sentences: DistractionTriggerReason (MonolithModels.kt:195) attaches a static coachingTip string to each intercept after it happens. There is no drill mode, no controlled exposure (surface the blocked app, hold the Airlock, score the resistance), no progression, and no resistance metric feeding session length or loadout choice. Pure avoidance means the skill never transfers: uninstall the app and the user is exactly as defenceless as on day one.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:195`

#### [HIGH] Face-down is the most natural focus gesture in the industry and Monolith cannot sense orientation at all

Benchmark: Google Pixel's Flip to Shhh (bundled with Digital Wellbeing) uses the accelerometer and gyroscope to detect the phone placed face-down on a flat surface and instantly engages Do Not Disturb; picking it back up releases it (support.google.com Pixel gestures page; Android Police). Forest's Deep Focus is the crude software cousin — the tree dies if you leave the app — proving users want the phone's physical state, not an app's foreground state, to carry the session. Monolith's state: no SensorManager, no accelerometer, no proximity, no gyroscope anywhere in the codebase (zero grep hits); its only posture-aware surface, AlwaysOnDeskClockOverlay in AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:70-98, does the opposite — it burns FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON assuming the phone sits face-up and watched. A 'flip to seal' gesture (face-down = session sealed, phone lifted face-up = the session knows) would fit Monolith's mechanical ritual identity perfectly and costs one sensor listener; instead arming remains a sequence of on-screen taps a pocket or a thumb-flick can perform or abandon.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:70-98`

#### [HIGH] Charger state is a free, proven automation trigger (Digital Wellbeing) and Monolith reads battery only as a threat to itself

Benchmark: Google Digital Wellbeing's Bedtime mode offers 'Turn on while charging' as a first-class trigger — plug in inside the bedtime window and grayscale + DND engage automatically, unplug and it releases (documented in Digital Wellbeing setup guides and Xiaomi/Google support pages). Charger state is a reliable, zero-habit proxy for 'I have put the phone down for the night / at my desk dock'. Monolith's state: the only battery code in the app is defensive — MonolithRepository.kt:656-663 isBatteryOptimizationIgnored() treats power purely as a threat to its own background survival, and the app registers exactly three BroadcastReceivers (MonolithBootReceiver, RoutineAlarmReceiver, ReleaseRetryReceiver) — none listens for ACTION_POWER_CONNECTED/DISCONNECTED. A SLEEP or desk routine that arms when the phone is docked on the charger and stands down when unplugged is unbuildable in the current code, even though Monolith already has routines and a SLEEP finish concept starving for a physical trigger.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithRepository.kt:656-663`

#### [HIGH] No cool-down taper: the seal drops from full lockdown to full unlock in one write

Apple Fitness+ treats Mindful Cooldown as a first-class workout type and Nike Training Club / Nike Run Club build a cool-down into every session — the taper is where the body is returned to baseline, not dropped. Monolith's ending is binary: disarmActiveSession (MonolithRepository.kt:2297-2355) flips isActive=false in a single updateSession write and the shield stops, so every LOCKED/PEEK app and every blocked site unlocks in the same instant the timer expires — precisely the rebound-binge moment. The only post-finish hold is ReceiptState.Detention (ReceiptState.kt:200-235), a 1,200-1,800ms UI rack delay before showing the slip, not a taper: no staged unlock (e.g. study/utility apps first, feeds last), no held-notification triage while still shielded, no breathing/settle interval, no intention-setting for the next block. Session physiology goes 100% blocked to 0% blocked in one frame.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithRepository.kt:2297`

#### [HIGH] No RPE or readiness log: the receipt measures the phone, never how hard the session felt

WHOOP pairs a 1-10 RPE scale with Recovery/Strain Target — each morning sleep/HRV/resting-HR produce a Recovery score that converts into a recommended strain range for that day, and Strava logs perceived exertion per activity so load can be calibrated. Monolith records only machine facts. FocusSessionEntity (MonolithModels.kt:268-380) has elapsed, penalty, interceptions (phantomReachesBlocked), tamper and outcome — no effort, urge-intensity, difficulty, sleep or readiness field exists anywhere in the schema. The receipt contract confirms it: PendingReceipt/ReceiptState (ReceiptState.kt:135-198) carry 18 fields — planned/elapsed seconds, heldApps/heldSites, deflections, shieldWasOff, bankedBreakSeconds — and not one subjective field. A brutal 50 minutes fought urge-by-urge on no sleep and an effortless 50 minutes on a rested morning therefore receipt, total and judge identically, and there is no signal with which any future progression or lighter day could be justified.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/ReceiptState.kt:135`

#### [HIGH] No wake-up ritual: the night ends in a binary 03:30 all-apps-reopen with no dawn release, alarm-linked end or morning sequence

Sleep Cycle's smart alarm wakes inside a light-sleep window instead of at a fixed instant, sunrise-simulation products brighten gradually over 20-30 minutes before wake time, and Digital Wellbeing Bedtime mode can 'deactivate at next alarm' so release is tied to the user's actual morning. Monolith has no wake side at all: the SLEEP routine simply ends at endMinutes=210 (03:30, MonolithRepository.kt:849-851) and every blocked app reopens simultaneously, with no staged morning unlock (essentials first, feeds last), no alarm Clock integration, no wake-window flexibility, and no morning intention/briefing step. The only thing 03:30 does in code is file history: DrawerDay.kt:8-27 uses the 210-minute offset purely as a bookkeeping boundary for 'which day' a task belongs to. The app that polices the night abandons the user at the single most relapse-prone moment — the first groggy minutes with a fully unlocked phone.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithRepository.kt:849-851; app/src/main/java/com/example/data/DrawerDay.kt:8-27`

#### [HIGH] Zero sleep audio: an elaborate sound engine that only plays clicks — no sleepcasts, soundscapes, guided wind-down or fade-out timer

Headspace's Sleep by Headspace is built on Sleepcasts (ever-changing narrated ambient journeys), sleep music, an 8-hour Sleep Radio and Nighttime SOS for mid-night waking; Pzizz similarly generates 'dreamscapes' mixing voice, music and effects with a fade-out. Monolith ships a sophisticated synth engine and uses it exclusively for mechanical feedback: TactileSoundEngine.kt exposes only playRotaryDetent, playFirmClick, playSeatKnock, playMechanicalLatch, playHarmonicSeal and playSealThrow (TactileSoundEngine.kt:629-800) — short clicks and latch sounds rendered on AudioTrack, with no ambient/soundscape player, no looping content, no sleep timer or volume fade-out, and no audio assets anywhere in the repo. The one coaching line in the codebase tells an intercepted user to 'Take one slow breath' as static text (MonolithModels.kt:203). A user who locks the phone at 20:00 and lies awake staring at the ceiling gets silence and a wall — no ritual content to actually fall asleep to, and nothing at all for a 2 a.m. waking.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/service/TactileSoundEngine.kt:629-800; app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:203`

#### [HIGH] No goal pot: focus minutes fund nothing named — no target, no progress-to-target, no completion date

Qapital is built around named Goals — a pot with a target (vacation, emergency fund) that rules fill and a visual progress tracker fills toward — and Monzo Pots do the same: named, separated pots, each with an optional target, a visible balance-versus-target progress bar and scheduled deposits. Monolith has no equivalent object at all: there is no goal/pot entity in the schema (MonolithModels.kt:100-793), and the design actively forbids one — FocusTaskEntity's own header comment (MonolithModels.kt:101-115) decrees a task is 'a name, torn off when done', stored with 0 = no estimate, because 'session length lives on the wheel, never on a task'. So 40 hours of exam preparation can never exist as a pot that is 340 minutes from full, with an on-pace/behind verdict and a projected completion date; every session funds nothing cumulative, it just evaporates into a one-slot receipt. Savings apps learned a decade ago that people persist for a named, filling container — Monolith offers a furnace with no account attached.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:101-115`

#### [HIGH] No rules engine: resisted urges and peeks trigger no automatic deposit or tax — Qapital's Round Up and Guilty Pleasure rituals have no analogue

Qapital's own rules page (qapital.com) ships an if-this-then-save engine: Round Up sweeps spare change per purchase (users average $44/month), Guilty Pleasure auto-saves a set amount every time you spend at the place you're resisting, Spend Less banks the difference when you come in under a merchant budget, and Set and Forget moves a fixed amount on a schedule — behaviour itself is the deposit trigger. #### [CRITICAL] No session soundscape exists: the engine is architecturally forbidden from making any sound longer than 160ms

Forest ships a library of Ambient Sounds (rain, cafe, meadow) layered over the focus session itself, with individual tracks purchasable in coins and rotating seasonal access on Plus; Opal's free tier includes Soundscapes. Monolith's sessions are sonically empty from seal to finish: the engine's own header legislates 'Zero ambient sound mixer loops' and 'Zero audio files in res/raw or assets/' (TactileSoundEngine.kt:29-31), the synth loop caps every render at a 0.16s transient buffer (TactileSoundEngine.kt runFloatPcmSynthLoop, maxSamples = SAMPLE_RATE * 0.16f) and enqueueTransient coerces duration to 96-6000 samples (~136ms max). There is no MediaPlayer, no raw/ assets, and no sustained-tone API anywhere in the file — the machinery physically cannot hold a sound for longer than a click, so a user focusing for 90 minutes hears exactly nothing the app makes.

### Head-to-head losses — 34 findings (11 critical, 20 high, 3 medium, 0 low)

_Against one sec, Monolith loses the friction category outright: it has no always-on intervention, only a single passive 5-second numeral inside pre-armed sessions, and none of the attempt-count feedback, intervention variety, escalation, or healthy-alternative redirects that make one sec's pause actually change behaviour._

#### [CRITICAL] No friction outside an armed session: one sec guards every open, Monolith guards only pre-planned hours

one sec (one-sec.app) inserts its intervention on every open of a flagged app, all day, with no session to arm — that always-on reflex-breaking is its entire product and its PNAS-reported 57% cut in opens. Monolith has zero friction outside a pre-planned sealed session or routine: MonolithAccessibilityService returns immediately when there is no active session ('val activeSession = dao.getActiveSessionSnapshot() ?: return@launch; if (!activeSession.isActive) return@launch'), and the shield monitor does the same. The unplanned evening/weekend reach — the majority of mindless opens — is never interrupted at all.

#### [CRITICAL] One passive numeral vs one sec's per-app intervention library: no guided breath, no active task, no adjustable or escalating length

one sec ships a per-app intervention library — guided deep breath, 4-7-8 breathing, Mirror (front camera), Rotate Phone, Type random text, Follow the Dot, Conversational Reflection, LENGO vocabulary (one-sec.app homepage) — with adjustable intervention length and an official 'gradually elongate interventions with each attempt' mode to defeat habituation. Monolith ships exactly one intervention for every app: a passive hardcoded 5-second countdown rendered as an 88sp numeral ('0%d'), with no breathing pacing or animation to follow, no active task to perform, and no setting anywhere for type, duration, or escalation — the user just watches a clock tick and learns to wait it out on autopilot.

Freedom Premium's $39.99/yr covers unlimited devices across Mac, Windows, iOS, Android and Chromebook with one synced session covering every screen at once, Opal Pro works on all the buyer's devices (iPhone, Mac, Android) at no extra cost, and Cold Turkey's $39-$45 one-time Pro key covers all of the buyer's own Windows and Mac machines. Monolith's value is stranded on a single handset: the project builds one Android app module only, ships no iOS, desktop or browser-extension client, and has no account system to carry any entitlement or rule set to a second device. Anyone whose distraction spans phone plus laptop must still buy Freedom, Opal or Cold Turkey in full - making Monolith's marginal value in a real multi-screen setup $0 regardless of its own price.

#### [MEDIUM] No launch-count (open-limit) blocking and no allowlist mode — two AppBlock rule types Monolith cannot express

AppBlock offers two rule shapes beyond time schedules: Launch count / Open limit (an app is blocked after N opens per day or hour, metering reflexive checking without a hard ban) and Allowlist mode (only chosen apps are usable, everything else is blocked). Both are rule types a switching user can build in AppBlock in minutes and cannot build in Monolith at all.

### Improvement backlog — 39 findings (13 critical, 20 high, 6 medium, 0 low)

_Build in this order — analytics/insights first (local, cheapest, proves value), then cross-device sync with a browser companion, then location/Wi-Fi/launch-count triggers, then partner accountability — because Monolith currently matches rivals only on the block itself and is missing every surrounding basic that makes users stay._

Build order #2 (after analytics, which needs no backend): account + synced blocklists/sessions + a Chrome extension first, desktop apps second.

### Visual design — 39 findings (6 critical, 23 high, 10 medium, 0 low)

_Monolith's type system is a telemetry terminal, not a designed product voice: two-weight families that force all-caps shouting, a proportional face on the live timer, no calm register for its signature intervention, and a brand name set at badge size — every polished rival (Opal's five-weight SF Pro system, one sec's prose intervention) wins on typography alone._

#### [CRITICAL] Zero-green, single-hue system: success, error and the primary CTA are all the same orange

Forest makes colour carry the verdict: a completed session is a vibrant green tree, a failed one a withered dead tree, in a calming green palette. Monolith bans that channel by doctrine — Color.kt:5-7 declares 'Strictly Zero-Green: Every single color satisfies green < maxOf(red, blue)', so no success/positive colour can ever exist. Worse, the remaining hues collapse into each other: the primary accent #F55314 (Color.kt:18) and the alert #D63E06 (Color.kt:19, 'deepest step of the ONE orange hue') are the same hue family, and at night Theme.kt:61 sets error = NightColorPrimaryContainer, i.e. an error is rendered in literally the accent colour. Blocked, danger, primary CTA and completion are chromatically indistinguishable; only text tells them apart.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/theme/Color.kt:5-19; app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/theme/Theme.kt:61`

#### [CRITICAL] No theme choice and no system-dark respect: night is imposed only by session/SLEEP routine, never chosen

Benchmark: StayFree advertises Dark mode as a headline feature and 13 themes; standard Android/Material 3 practice is Light/Dark/Follow-system via isSystemInDarkTheme(). Monolith: grep finds zero isSystemInDarkTheme calls; MonolithViewModel.kt:212 comment states 'The manual theme is DEAD... _darkTheme and toggleTheme() are deleted with the DAY/NIGHT pill', and evaluateTheme() at MonolithViewModel.kt:70-97 returns night ONLY when a session is active or a SLEEP routine owns the hour. A user with system dark mode on at 14:00 gets the light scheme; a user who wants permanent dark outside sessions cannot have it. Dark is a punishment state the app imposes, never a preference it respects.

### Student life — 36 findings (13 critical, 18 high, 5 medium, 0 low)

_Monolith has no timetable at all — only hand-typed weekly alarms — while rivals sync the calendar, model the school week day-by-day, and stand down for holidays, so a student must rebuild their class schedule by hand inside the app and keep it true forever or be blocked and judged against a timetable that no longer exists._

#### [CRITICAL] No calendar or ICS integration: the student's real timetable lives elsewhere and Monolith can never see it

Benchmarks: Samsung Modes and Routines offers 'Event: From your calendar' as an automatic turn-on condition for a focus mode; Opal advertises calendar-driven automated schedules ('Calendar: set daily working hours, sleep and routines, block apps automatically') plus calendar-synced work schedules in Pro; Apple Focus ships Calendar focus filters and schedule/automation triggers. Monolith: AndroidManifest.xml:5-13 declares no READ_CALENDAR (and no location) permission, and there is zero CalendarContract, calendar ContentResolver query, or .ics/file import anywhere in app/src/main/java — the only schedule source is routines typed by hand into ShieldMatrixScreen. A university timetable already exists in Google Calendar and as an ICS feed from the school portal; Monolith forces a manual retype, after which the two silently drift — a cancelled lecture, a room/time change, or a special exam timetable never propagates, and the app keeps enforcing the stale copy.

Location: `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:5-13`

#### [CRITICAL] The routine model cannot express a school timetable: one window, one day-mask, one loadout, no subject, no per-day lessons

Benchmarks: Google Family Link School Time is edited as a weekly school timetable — set each school day's start/end individually, apply per day; YPT (Yeolpumta) tracks study time per subject and organises the day around subjects. Monolith: RoutineEntity (MonolithModels.kt:550-570) is exactly name + startMinutes + endMinutes + a 7-bit daysMask + one loadoutName — no subject, no per-day differing times, no alternating Week A/B rotation, no link to tasks or stats. The shipped defaults prove the ceiling: MonolithRepository.kt:839-853 seeds one 'DAY BLOCKS' 09:00-19:30 ALL_DAYS slab rather than any class day. A real timetable (Mon 09:00 Maths, 11:00 Physics; Tue completely different) can only be faked by exploding it into dozens of disconnected generic routines, and ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:328-336 renders them as a flat list of start→end rows — there is no weekly grid, no today timeline, no 'next class' view anywhere in the app.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:550-570`

#### [CRITICAL] No exam date or D-Day exists — test days are explicitly designed out of the app

YPT (Yeolpumta) ships a D-Day counter for exam/assessment dates, surfaced even on its Wear OS complication alongside today's study total. The data to learn from is also thrown away: tasks carry categoryTag (MonolithModels.kt:113) but compute7DayHistory (MonolithRepository.kt:2359-2395) aggregates only undifferentiated totalMinutes and a blocks25 count — no per-subject totals exist anywhere, so a student can never see they did 4h of Maths and 20 minutes of Biology all week.

### Everyday use — 40 findings (11 critical, 21 high, 8 medium, 0 low)

_Monolith has no home-screen presence whatsoever — no start widget, no live countdown widget, no stats widget, no QS tile — while one sec, Opal, AppBlock and even Digital Wellbeing all live on the home screen, leaving Monolith invisible at the exact moments of temptation and intent it exists for._

#### [CRITICAL] No home-screen widget exists at all — starting a focus session always requires opening the app

Benchmark: one sec's own tutorial (tutorials.one-sec.app) documents starting a manual block 'directly from your Home Screen' via its home-screen widget, without opening the app; Opal's store listing advertises 'Widget: Have Opal on your home screen!'; even the small rival Otol ships a 'Home-screen widget: today's focus total and one-tap start'. Monolith: zero widget stack — no AppWidgetProvider class, no RemoteViews or AppWidgetManager reference anywhere in app/src/main/java, no res/layout directory at all, and no glance/appwidget dependency in app/build.gradle.kts or gradle/libs.versions.toml (grep returns nothing). Every session must be started by opening the app and working the in-app Deck/dial flow, adding friction at the exact moment of intent that rivals have engineered down to one home-screen tap.

#### [CRITICAL] No delegated lock: no partner approval, held PIN or change-cooldown — the person tempted to cheat is the only keyholder

AppBlock ships Strict Mode change-locking behind a cooldown or required third-party approval, and StayFree requires a password to change any app settings — both exist because the craving self must not hold the only key. #### [CRITICAL] No non-motor alternative: starting, and escaping, both demand precision drags and a 60-second sustained hold

Monolith honours the system animator scale in exactly one place — a single Strike animation snaps instead of tweening when ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE==0 (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:807-816) — and nowhere else: the PARK drawer throws/seats (ParkDrawer.kt:150-156), the seal throw, rotary settle animators and sled throws all run regardless, and PARK offers no in-app reduce-motion toggle. A vestibular or migraine user who has not zeroed the global animator scale gets the full motion show on every interaction.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/components/MonolithCustomComponents.kt:807-816; app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/components/ParkDrawer.kt:150-156`

#### [HIGH] Appearance is not the user's: theme toggle was deliberately deleted, sessions force night, and no high-contrast option exists

Rivals and the platform leave appearance to the user/system: one sec declares Dark Interface and Sufficient Contrast as supported features following the system, and Android itself offers user-chosen dark theme, high-contrast text and colour correction. Monolith deliberately abolished user choice — MonolithViewModel.kt:212-214 states 'The manual theme is DEAD... toggleTheme() are deleted' and darkTheme is 'DERIVED from the evaluation, never stored, never toggled' (lines 474-479); Theme.kt:108 forces SealedVaultNightColorScheme whenever a session is active, MainActivity.kt:105 hardcodes dynamicColor=false and never reads isSystemInDarkTheme(), and PARK's THEME row (ParkDrawer.kt:602-623) is a printed readout, not a control. There is no light option during a night routine/session and no high-contrast scheme at all, so a low-vision user who reads dark-on-light is forced onto Monolith's low-step night staircase (Color.kt:36, surfaceBright only 1.35:1 over ground) for the entire focus session.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/MonolithViewModel.kt:212-214,474-479; app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/theme/Theme.kt:102-113; app/src/main/java/com/example/MainActivity.kt:103-115`

#### [HIGH] One phone equals one person in the data model: two regular users of one handset cannot be separated

Benchmarks: Google Family Link gives each child their own profile with their own limits, approvals and reports, and Samsung Kids supports up to six separate child profiles on one handset. Monolith's schema has no person dimension at all: FocusSessionEntity (MonolithModels.kt:268) carries intention/profileName but no owner or user field, GuardSettingsEntity is a single hard-coded row (@PrimaryKey id = 1, MonolithModels.kt:745), and EmergencyBreakSpendEntity (:443) makes the one weekly emergency token device-global. On a handset regularly shared by two people — partners, siblings, parent and teen — both people's sessions, receipts, day words, statistics and the single weekly token merge into one indivisible record, and one person's emergency spend silently consumes the other's.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:268, :443, :745`

#### [HIGH] No kid-safe handover space: no curated child home, approved contacts or child budget on the shared phone

Benchmark: Samsung Kids replaces the home screen with a contained space showing only parent-approved apps, a parental-PIN exit, approved-contacts-only calling, its own daily playtime limit and per-child usage reports. Monolith offers nothing between 'full phone' and 'focus session': its only per-app concept is the owner's focus tier on BlockedAppEntity (MonolithModels.kt:232, OPEN/PEEK/LOCKED), the manifest declares no alternate/kid launcher or home activity (AndroidManifest.xml:20, :48 — MainActivity is the sole LAUNCHER entry), and there is no approved-contacts calling, no child time budget separate from the session dial, and no child usage report. Outside a session a child handed the phone gets the owner's entire device; inside one they get an Airlock written for adult urges, complete with a weekly-token emergency valve.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:232; app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:20`

#### [HIGH] No tablet or large-screen life: stretched phone UI, no two-pane design, no shared state

Benchmarks: Opal ships a native iPad app (plus Mac), Freedom treats a tablet as a full member of a synced session, and Apple Screen Time syncs settings across iPhone, iPad and Mac on the same account. Monolith contains zero large-screen adaptation: no WindowSizeClass or window-size logic anywhere in app/src/main/java, no sw600dp/landscape resource qualifiers (app/src/main/res/ contains only values and values-night), and its navigation is a fixed phone rail/scaffold in MainActivity.kt. Installed on an Android tablet or foldable — a primary study device for the student audience this app targets — it renders as a stretched single-column phone UI, and because there is no sync (see cross-device finding) the tablet does not even inherit the phone's blocklists, routines or history.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/MainActivity.kt:409; app/src/main/res/ (no sw600dp or land qualifiers)`

#### [MEDIUM] Widget-shaped hole extends to every adjacent surface: no Quick Settings tile and no launcher shortcuts either

Benchmark: AppBlock documents a Quick Block Quick Settings tile to 'start or stop Quick Block with a single tap from anywhere'; one sec additionally offers a Control Center toggle and Shortcuts-app actions for starting blocks. Monolith offers none of these surfaces: the manifest declares no TileService and no app-shortcut meta-data, and res/xml contains no shortcuts.xml — grep for TileService, RemoteViews and AppWidgetManager across app/src/main/java returns zero hits. The app's entire presence outside its own activity is a launcher icon; a user mid-task in another app who wants to arm a block must context-switch into Monolith's full UI instead of tapping a tile.

#### [MEDIUM] No external intent or automation contract: system Modes, routines and Tasker cannot trigger Monolith

Benchmark: Opal advertises Shortcut Integration to 'start/stop Focus Sessions based on app opens, time, location and more', and Digital Wellbeing Focus mode is integrated into Android's system Modes Quick Settings tile. Monolith: MainActivity.kt:121-143 consumes only its own intercept intent (onNewIntent even drops re-intercepts while alive) and the manifest declares no custom VIEW/START action, deep link or automation intent-filter — Tasker, Samsung/Google Modes, Assistant Routines and NFC triggers have no entry point to arm a session, so Monolith can never participate in the phone-wide routines users already run.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/MainActivity.kt:121-143`

#### [MEDIUM] Zero Wear OS presence: no watch app, tile or complication — the wrist glance does not exist

Benchmark: StayFree ships Wear OS support and advertises a widget for quick access to usage info on wearable devices (Play/store listings), so its users can check time state from the wrist. Monolith is a single-module phone app: settings.gradle.kts:27 includes only ':app', AndroidManifest.xml declares no wearable declarations, and there is no TileService, complication data source or watch companion anywhere in the tree. A Wear OS owner gets literally nothing on the wrist — no remaining-time glance, no session state, no quick start — and must pull out and unlock the phone, the highest-friction possible 'glance' for the device class whose entire purpose is glanceability.

#### [MEDIUM] No pre-routine heads-up: scheduled blocks begin with no advance notification or countdown glance anywhere outside the app

Benchmark: ScreenZen's current release ships 'Halo heads-up: a quiet countdown before a scheduled Halo block' — an out-of-app warning that a block is about to begin. Monolith's scheduled routines have no equivalent at any point: grep finds zero occurrences of 'Notification' in both RoutineAlarmReceiver.kt and RoutineScheduler.kt, so when a routine window opens the first externally visible signal is the shield notification after blocking has already started. A user mid-conversation, mid-navigation or mid-payment gets ambushed by a block they could have been warned about minutes earlier with a glanceable countdown; rivals treat the pre-block warning as a shipped feature, Monolith treats it as nothing.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/service/RoutineAlarmReceiver.kt`

#### [MEDIUM] Allowlist granularity stops at the package: no function-level modes (messages-only, feed-off) inside multi-purpose apps

ScreenZen's Minimal mode lets users keep Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and Reddit installed and openable while removing Reels, Shorts and endless feeds, including messages-only options — the allowlist is drawn inside the app, per function. Monolith's entire in-app granularity is one hardcoded detector for Shorts/Reels view IDs in exactly two packages (MonolithAccessibilityService.kt:332-348, youtube/instagram IDs only), armed by a single global on/off flag for all contexts (MonolithAccessibilityService.kt:112-115, shortsSniperArmed; GuardSettingsEntity shortsReelsSniperEnabled). There is no per-app or per-loadout choice and no equivalent for the functions real life actually splits on — Instagram DMs without the feed, YouTube search/subscriptions without Shorts, WhatsApp calls without chats — every other app is whole-package LOCKED, PEEK_2M or OPEN (MonolithModels.kt:13-40).

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/service/MonolithAccessibilityService.kt:112-115; app/src/main/java/com/example/service/MonolithAccessibilityService.kt:332-348`

#### [MEDIUM] Routine ends are computed as start-plus-duration, so overnight windows end an hour early or late in local time on DST transition nights

Apple Focus/Sleep, Google Digital Wellbeing Bedtime and Freedom recurring sessions all specify a schedule by two local clock times, so a 23:00-07:00 block ends at 07:00 local on every night of the year. Monolith stores endMinutes but its derivation collapses it into a duration once (MonolithModels.kt:578) and then computes every window end as epoch arithmetic — 'val end = start + durMs' in both nextEndMillis (MonolithModels.kt:605-622) and windowContaining. On the spring-forward night an overnight window lifts an hour early in local terms; on the fall-back night it runs an hour long — precisely the sleep/work windows where an hour of unexpected unblocking or over-blocking is most visible, and the user is never told the end time moved.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:605-622`

#### [MEDIUM] No graduated strictness: no friction-only or cancellable tier — every session is maximum hardness or nothing

Opal offers three difficulty levels — Normal (cancel anytime), Timeout (increasing delays before snoozing) and Deep Focus (unreachable until the timer ends) — and one sec / ScreenZen sell configurable delay-only friction as a complete, retainable tier for users who need a pause, not a wall. Monolith has one hardness: StudyModePreset at MonolithModels.kt:61-68 varies only duration and block count, and every arm goes through the same seal, the same grace cliff and the same weekly-token valve. A user who discovers hard blocking is too much for daily life has no lighter mode to step down to inside the app — the only downgrade available is uninstalling and moving to a friction-first rival.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:61`

#### [MEDIUM] No watch companion: checking your session means unlocking the phone you are trying not to use

Benchmarks: Forest ships a Watch app alongside iOS/Android/browser; Routinery carries routines from phone to Apple Watch, tablet and Mac; Apple Focus mirrors automatically to Apple Watch, so remaining time and session state are visible without touching the phone. Monolith has no Wear OS module, tile, complication or Data Layer code — grep for wear/wearable/horologist across gradle/libs.versions.toml and app/build.gradle.kts returns nothing. The only thing named 'Watch' in the codebase is WatchStore (app/src/main/java/com/example/service/WatchStore.kt:147), an internal permission-stamp store with no connection to any wearable. To check how long is left in a session, the user must pick up, unlock and stare at the exact device the session exists to keep them off.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/service/WatchStore.kt:147; gradle/libs.versions.toml (no wearable dependencies)`

### Flows and friction — 40 findings (8 critical, 21 high, 11 medium, 0 low)

_From install, Monolith demands maximum trust, maximum configuration and a 100-minute default commitment before delivering any value, while Forest, Opal, AppBlock and StayFree each deliver a first win — a planted tree, an auto-built schedule, or 10 days of personal usage insight — in under a minute._

#### [CRITICAL] No permission-free first win: no trial/demo session exists, and the very first arm is hard-gated on a LIVE warrant

Forest ships value with zero special permissions and zero configuration: reviews document it 'works offline with almost no setup' and 'don't require setup or onboarding — you can start with a single focus session' by setting a timer and pressing Start. Monolith has no trial, demo or permission-free mode at all (no demo/trial/quick-start code exists in app/src/main/java). Its only path to a first win is the slide-to-arm, and SlideGestureMath.commits() returns true only when the warrant state is LIVE (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1352-1353), i.e. after the accessibility/usage grants are in place; the slide is wired to that warrantProvider in TactileDeckScreen.kt:997. A new user who grants nothing gets literally nothing — not even a simulated Airlock intercept to feel the product before handing over the most sensitive permission Android has.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:1352`

#### [CRITICAL] No degraded-mode track: refusing Accessibility is all-or-nothing, rivals let you run on Usage Access alone

one sec (Android) ships an explicit degraded track: on its permission request screen, 'Learn more' -> 'ignore accessibility service' drops the user to a usage-access-only legacy mode, because 'it's better than not being able to use one sec at all' (tutorials.one-sec.app). Monolith has no fallback track at any level: WatchStore.deriveWarrant (app/src/main/java/com/example/service/WatchStore.kt:296) is a hard conjunction — !a11yBound -> OFF, usage DENIED -> OFF — and the only onboarding response to a refusal is the same FIX key looping the user back to the same Settings pane (ParkDrawer.kt:412-458). A user who balks at the single scariest permission in Android gets zero product, forever, instead of a slower polling-only blocker.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/service/WatchStore.kt:296; app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/components/ParkDrawer.kt:412`

#### [CRITICAL] No extend-session: a session in flow cannot add time, only die and be re-armed from zero

Cold Turkey Micromanager 1.3 (getcoldturkey.com release notes, 23 Dec 2025) added a one-tap 'extend blocks by 10 minutes during a timed block', and Cold Turkey Blocker's timer lock likewise lets a running block be extended. Monolith has no such verb anywhere: targetDurationSeconds is set once in startSession (MonolithRepository.kt:1321-1350), baked into the HMAC payload (CryptoIntegrityManager.kt:57-60) and never mutated by any repository function. The only 'extend' in the app, extendActiveTaskOvertime (MonolithViewModel.kt:1814-1825) calling extendTaskEstimate (MonolithRepository.kt:2511), raises a task's estimate by 5 minutes and pointedly does not touch the session — when a session is active it does not even sync the dial. A user in flow at expiry is hard-cut, receipted, and must re-run the full slide-to-arm and proving flow for a new session instead of tapping +10 once.

Location: `MonolithRepository.kt:1321-1350; MonolithViewModel.kt:1814-1825`

#### [CRITICAL] No pause/resume: the session clock and shield can never freeze and resume, so any real-life interruption costs the whole session

Google Digital Wellbeing Focus mode offers 'Take a break' from its notification to unpause apps for a short period and then resume the same mode; Opal (non-Deep Focus) lets you pause a session to allow specific apps for a set time and purpose; AppBlock lets a non-Strict user open the app and pause/edit the active schedule mid-block. Monolith's FocusSessionEntity (MonolithModels.kt:270-296) has no paused flag, pause anchor or paused-accumulation field at all, and a codebase-wide search finds no pauseSession/pause verb for a session — elapsed is derived continuously from monotonic anchors in updateSessionProgress (MonolithRepository.kt:1934+), so the clock never freezes. The Safe Break is not a pause: it fires only automatically at a block boundary in multi-block sessions (MonolithRepository.kt:2020-2035), never on demand mid-block. A doorbell, call or delivery mid-session therefore either burns counted focus time or forces the 60-second Emergency Break Valve, which ends the session entirely and spends the one weekly token.

Location: `MonolithModels.kt:270-296; MonolithRepository.kt:1934-2035`

#### [CRITICAL] No settings home, no settings search, and the settings drawer is an unlabelled wordless zone

Benchmark: AppBlock documents a breadcrumb path for every preference under one named home (Profile → Customize → Blocking preferences / Notifications → Statistics), Opal support directs users to a named 'Settings -> Autofocus -> Autofocus overlay' path, and Android/iOS Settings put a search bar on top that jumps to any setting by keyword. Monolith has no settings destination at all: the rail offers only DECK/SHIELD/TASKS/VAULT (MainActivity.kt:718-721), the word 'Settings' never appears in any UI file, and the only searches in the app filter apps (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:452 'Filter apps…') or old tasks (DrawerScreen.kt). The closest thing to a settings sheet, PARK, is reached through a 48dp rail zone that by design 'prints NO word ever' (MonolithRailView.kt:79-80), so a user hunting for any setting must already know an unlabelled gesture target exists, then guess which of PARK vs SHIELD vs the Drawer hides the control.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/views/MonolithRailView.kt:79-80; app/src/main/java/com/example/MainActivity.kt:718-721`

#### [CRITICAL] No lockout-recovery flow exists: no help surface, no cooldown/charger/trusted-contact unlock, no support code — zero tokens means zero verbs

AppBlock ships a dedicated Emergency Unblocking flow: in-app at Profile > Help > Contact support, with multiple self-serve unlock conditions (PIN, charger plug-in, timer expiry, cooldown wait, trusted Approval Contact) and a one-time support unlock code that disables Strict Mode and resets a forgotten PIN. Monolith has no equivalent of any of it: no help, support, contact or FAQ surface exists anywhere in the codebase, no cooldown/delayed-unlock request a user can file to start a clock, no charger or trusted-contact proof. The disarm overlay is the whole recovery design, and at zero tokens it renders nothing at all — AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:781 gates the valve on tokensRemaining > 0 — so a user who mis-locked an essential app (authenticator, dialler, maps) has literally zero verbs left except waiting out the session or routine window.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:732-790`

#### [CRITICAL] At the moment of temptation the app speaks telemetry, not persuasion: no reflective question, no breath cue, no user-written or tone-chosen block message exists

Freedom ships customizable block screens: seven tones from tough love to encouragement, or a fully user-written message, explicitly 'a reminder of why you're blocking an app in the first place'; one sec lets users replace its breathing prompt ('It's time to take a deep breath…') with a personal one and labels its choices in plain first person ('I don't want to open Instagram' / 'Continue to Instagram'); ScreenZen's pause asks 'Is this important?'; Opal's Mindful Block Screens rotate quotes and puns. Monolith's intercept offers none of this: the headline is a system event, 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • {badge}' (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:606), the centre is an 88sp countdown numeral (:635), the only personal line is a data label, 'ACTIVE INTENTION: …' (:647-654), and the only verbs are RETURN TO FOCUS / EMERGENCY PEEK (:657-686). A codebase-wide search finds no setting for block-screen text, tone, quote or reminder anywhere — the words spoken at the exact moment of temptation are fixed, authorial and about the machine, never about the user's reason.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:606-686`

#### [CRITICAL] No gesture teach-in at all: a five-gesture bespoke vocabulary is shipped with its only glossary hidden inside a drawer users cannot yet open

Benchmarks teach their one core gesture in-flow: Opal's Help Center flow ends with a labelled 'Hold to Commit' that visibly turns into 'Committed', Forest puts a bright green dot handle on the dial's track next to a labelled Plant button, and ScreenZen walks users step-by-step through setup including its gesture unlock. Monolith instead ships at least five invented gestures — rotate-and-throw the wheel, tap invisible hub wells, slide-or-tap with a catch/refusal stop, drag a rail cap, flick a sled — with zero coach marks, demo animation, first-use overlay or tutorial anywhere in code (no hint/tutorial/onboarding code exists). The only gesture glossary in the app is two lines of a spec plate, 'WHEEL SETS TIME · SLIDE ARMS · THE HOLD BREAKS', buried inside the PARK drawer the user must already have discovered how to open.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/components/ParkDrawer.kt:108-117; app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:685,983`

#### [HIGH] First-session default is a 100-minute commitment (50 min × 2 blocks), with no short starter session offered

The out-of-box ask is a ~100-minute commitment before the user has felt a single second of value: MonolithViewModel.kt:217 defaults _dialMinutes to 50 and :220 defaults _studyBlocksCount to 2, with the POMODORO_25_5 preset name contradicting both. Forest's first session is one short timer the user picks in seconds; Opal markets 'Get Started in Minutes: connect to Screen Time and choose your most distracting apps' with a recommended schedule auto-created for the first 24 hours. Monolith offers no 5- or 10-minute starter session, no 'try a short one first' ramp — the dial can go to 3 minutes (MonolithViewModel.kt:1472) but nothing in the first-run flow ever suggests or pre-arms it, so the default first experience is the longest plausible one.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/MonolithViewModel.kt:217`

#### [HIGH] No instant retrospective insight: existing UsageStats history is queried for only 12h and never shown to the new user

AppBlock states that 'on a fresh installation, AppBlock can retrieve up to 10 days of history' and turns it into an Insights aha (Usage categorisation, pickups, longest focus) before any blocking is configured; StayFree likewise opens on real today/yesterday/7-day usage. Monolith already holds the same data source but wastes it: MonolithRepository.queryRealTodayUsageMinutes() (MonolithRepository.kt:534-545) queries only the trailing 12 hours and uses the result solely to populate catalogue usage numbers during seed-sync — no screen ever presents the new user with 'here is what your phone already says about your last week' as a first-minute payoff. The first personalised insight arrives only after the user has configured everything and completed a full session.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithRepository.kt:534`

#### [HIGH] Permission wall fires cold at first composition, before any goal, app pick or session exists to justify it

Opal earns its permission: its onboarding asks personalization questions, generates a personalized Focus Report ('17 years of your life on your phone'), surfaces the user's problem apps automatically from Screen Time data, and only then asks for Screen Time authorization and trial — reviewers clock a configured first session in under three minutes. Monolith inverts the order: at first composition, before the user has expressed any intent, chosen any app, or set any goal, a LaunchedEffect auto-opens PARK purely because the store has never measured (app/src/main/java/com/example/MainActivity.kt:315-319, parkIntroPending). The first thing a new user meets is a 9-line GUARD board of grant states for a product they have not yet decided they want — maximum cost предъявed at minimum motivation.

#### [HIGH] Onboarding never completes: the final grant earns a silent click, no proof test and no route to a first session

Opal's published setup flow ends in action, not status: step 2 is 'schedule a session', step 3 is 'Enjoy — Opal will automatically follow your schedule and block apps', and new users are pushed into a first 10-minute focus session as their first challenge. Monolith's flow has no terminal step at all: when a FIX trip actually repairs a grant, ParkDrawer's return effect deliberately celebrates nothing — 'The repaired line alone gets the firm click; the hand goes back in silence — no word prints, ever' (app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/components/ParkDrawer.kt:191-211) — and when the last grant lands the FIX key simply vanishes. Nothing then says 'open Instagram and watch it get intercepted', nothing routes the user to arm a first session, nothing proves the six Settings trips bought anything. Setup ends in a spreadsheet going quiet.

#### [HIGH] No quick duration pick: preset tiles were deleted, leaving only a precision rotary wheel between intent and start

Benchmark: Opal presents preset durations (5/10/60 minutes) and Forest is set-the-timer-then-tap-Plant; Monolith deliberately deleted its preset tiles — TactileDeckScreen.kt:569 'The preset tiles are gone: one value, one control — the wheel' — leaving a 288dp RotaryWheelView as the sole duration control, stepped at 9 degrees per 5 minutes (BlockitCoreViews.kt:524-530 valueForAngle). The four ready-made presets in MonolithModels.kt:69-72 (25m Sprint, 50m Deep, 90m Exam) are dead: StudyModePreset.* is referenced only for the STOPWATCH_FLOW pill at TactileDeckScreen.kt:722, never as duration chips, so reaching 25 minutes from the 50 default is always a precision circular drag, never a tap.

#### [HIGH] Default start commits to a 110-minute session that contradicts the app's own 25-minute preset

#### [HIGH] Starting requires a precision slide-to-0.92 gesture; there is no plain Start button like every rival's one-tap commit

Benchmark: Freedom advertises 'Quick Block: tap once to block apps and websites right away', Opal's Block Now is a one-tap immediate session, and Forest starts on a single Plant/Start tap. Monolith has no Start button at all: commit requires dragging the cap to displayed 0.84 under contact with damping past the 0.68 gate (finger coordinate p=0.92), per the SlideToStartView spec at BlockitCoreViews.kt:1410-1446, dispatching only at the latch frame (BlockitCoreViews.kt:2348). The tap shortcut is equally gated — cap-only hit area, a press under 90ms is rejected as a 'brush' with zero travel, and a second touch aborts the mesh — so the single most frequent action in the app demands a full-attention, full-track gesture every time.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:1410`

#### [HIGH] Temporary unlock is a single fixed 120-second recipe: no choosing 5/10 minutes, no extending a peek that needs slightly longer

one sec's Delayed Interventions (tutorials.one-sec.app, v4.1) kick the user out after a user-set interval and then let them 'select how much more time you'll need on the target app'; ScreenZen lets the user set the unlock duration per app (Play listing reviews cite unlocking for 7 minutes); Opal's pause is explicitly for a set amount of time and a specific purpose. Monolith's temporary access is one fixed recipe for every app, purpose and moment: PEEK_DURATION_SECONDS = 120 and PEEK_COOLDOWN_MILLIS = 20 minutes are compile-time constants (MonolithRepository.kt:106-108), start2MinutePeek in MonolithViewModel.kt grants exactly that lease, and there is no duration picker, no purpose, and no way to extend a peek that turns out to need 4 minutes to finish a login, reply or verification — the user waits out a 20-minute cooldown or kills the session.

Location: `MonolithRepository.kt:106-108`

#### [HIGH] End flow has no check-in: no 'did you do it?', rating, or note — session closes on machine facts only

Focusmate's end flow is a structured check-in: partners share how the session went and what they accomplished and celebrate progress (Focusmate help: Step 3 'Celebrate your progress'); one sec ships an Emotion/Intention Tracker and Journaling. Monolith's end is read-only: ReceiptSheet(receipt, onDismiss) at app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:56-59 has no input, rating or note callback, and ReceiptState at app/src/main/java/com/example/data/ReceiptState.kt:166-186 has no accomplished/rating/reflection field — the machine records deflections, the user never records whether the intention was met.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:56`

#### [HIGH] Receipt is context-free: no today total, goal progress, streak delta, or comparison at the completion moment

### Purpose and positioning — 37 findings (14 critical, 19 high, 4 medium, 0 low)

_Monolith has no category: it is a phone-only, solo, friction-and-wall hybrid doing five jobs its own plan file said belong to other apps, in a market where every winner owns exactly one job, on every screen, with other people watching._

#### [CRITICAL] No category: blocker, friction app, timer, task planner, routine judge and ledger in one body — its own ruling says blocker-only and the code disobeys it

Every rival owns exactly one named job: one sec is the breathing pause before an app opens (and markets a PNAS/Max Planck study showing a 57% cut in app opens), ScreenZen is free friction, Forest is the gamified focus timer, Freedom is the cross-device blocker, Opal is scheduled focus sessions plus a focus score. Monolith is all of them at once and therefore none: its four screens are a session deck (TactileDeckScreen.kt), a task planner (FocusSequencerScreen.kt), an app/site blocker (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt) and a history ledger (DrawerScreen.kt), plus routines that judge windows HELD/MISSED like a study tracker and a notification vault. Its own plan file already ruled on this and the code ignored the ruling: studio/plan/GUARD-RULING-AND-DRAWER.md:118 states 'Monolith is a blocker. It is not his study tracker. Study tracking remains YPT's and GMC's job' — yet the shipped app still sequences tasks, grades routine attendance and keeps the ledger. A user, a store listing or a reviewer cannot answer 'what category is this?' in one word, and an app with no category gets compared against the best product in each of the five it half-enters.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/screens/ (TactileDeckScreen.kt, FocusSequencerScreen.kt, ShieldMatrixScreen.kt, DrawerScreen.kt); studio/plan/GUARD-RULING-AND-DRAWER.md:118`

#### [CRITICAL] Phone-only in a category that has gone cross-device: no laptop, browser or second-screen presence at all

The category's centre of gravity is now cross-device: Freedom syncs one session across Mac, Windows, iOS, Android, Chromebook and Linux ('blocking a site on your phone also blocks it on your laptop'), Opal runs iOS/Android/macOS, and even friction-only one sec covers iOS, Android and desktop browsers. Monolith is a single Gradle module — settings.gradle.kts contains only include(":app") — with one Android applicationId (app/build.gradle.kts:16, com.aistudio.monolith.kxtpzr) and no desktop, web, browser-extension or iOS surface anywhere in the tree. Distraction is not phone-shaped: the moment the phone is blocked, the same feed is one laptop lid away, and every serious rival treats that switch as the core problem. Monolith competes in 'phone blocker' while the market sells 'attention everywhere'.

Location: `settings.gradle.kts (include(":app") only); app/build.gradle.kts:16`

#### [CRITICAL] No one job: it is simultaneously a timer, blocker, task manager, routine court and ledger — and therefore ownable as none of them

Benchmarks each name one failure mode in one sentence: one sec = breathing pause before a flagged app opens (57% fewer opens in its Heidelberg/Max Planck study), ScreenZen = free friction, Opal = scheduled hard sessions, Forest = grow a tree or it dies, Freedom = one blocklist on every device. Monolith's own metadata.json:1-3 sells only hardware metaphor — 'rotary sun dial, live 3-stop switchboard, slide-to-latch bar, knock pass, inked stamps' — with no outcome, user, or failure mode, and the code splits equally across four unrelated jobs (MonolithViewModel.kt:48-52: DECK focus timer, TASKS sequencer, SHIELD blocker, VAULT receipts) plus routines, notification-holding and a task ledger. No hero mechanic exists to recommend, remember, or search for.

Location: `metadata.json:1-3; app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/MonolithViewModel.kt:48-52`

#### [CRITICAL] It refuses the feedback loop on principle: no score, streak, garden or progress record to come back for

Opal's job is visible progress (Focus Score, weekly reports, streaks/gems, friend comparison), Forest's is a garden that accumulates every session, YPT's is subject stats with a heatmap that deepens as you study plus realtime ranking. Monolith explicitly legislates the opposite in DrawerScreen.kt:60-62: 'It is not a dashboard, report card or attendance book: no totals, no streaks, no percentages, no counts, no summons.' A sealed session therefore produces a single disposable receipt and then filing-cabinet storage — there is no cumulative asset, score, garden, or history curve whose growth gives a user a reason to start tomorrow's session, which is the retention engine every rival is built on.

Monolith's own store description in metadata.json calls it a 'tactile pocket switchboard and daybook' — not a blocker — and the code backs that up: 4 rail destinations that are 4 different product categories (MonolithViewModel.kt:48-52 DECK=Focus timer, SHIELD=blocker matrix, TASKS=task manager, VAULT=Receipts/journal), 11 Room entities spanning tasks, profiles, routines, blocked sites, captured notifications, day notes and emergency-break spends (MonolithModels.kt:100,231,251,267,442,451,462,543,549,744,793), and a 2,548-line ViewModel with 111 functions. No surface, listing or first-run can state what this app is for, so it loses the store-search and word-of-mouth contest to every rival that can.

#### [CRITICAL] The ritual key never leaves the tempting device: no physical token, NFC object, or off-phone anchor exists

Brick sells a $59 battery-free NFC puck: tap the phone to it to block, tap again to unblock, and users deliberately leave it in another room so exit requires standing up and walking to a physical object; one puck is shared across a household's phones. Monolith simulates that physicality in pixels only — RotaryWheelView (BlockitCoreViews.kt:371) and SlideToStartView (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1444), seal-throw and latch sounds in TactileSoundEngine.kt — while every release path (slide, 60s valve hold, peek chip) is another tap on the same phone that holds the distractions. There is no NFC, tag, or external-token code anywhere in app/src/main and AndroidManifest.xml declares no NFC permission or feature: the 'key' and the temptation live in the same hand, so the ritual collapses to willpower with better sound effects.

#### [CRITICAL] Not for parents, guardians or schools: the blocked person is the administrator — there is no second person in the model

Apple Screen Time via Family Sharing and Google Family Link let a parent set limits, approve apps and remotely lock a child's device from the parent's own device — the rule-setter and the blocked person are different people with different credentials. Monolith has no role separation at all: every entity is ownerless and single-person (FocusSessionEntity, MonolithModels.kt:267-300, carries intention/duration/HMAC but no owner, subject or guardian field), there is no account, parent PIN, companion app or remote control anywhere in the codebase, and the only exit is self-administered by the blocked person himself (the 60s self-hold valve, MonolithViewModel.kt:195 and ParkDrawer.kt:111 'ONE BREAK A WEEK'). A parent who installs this on a child's phone has handed the child the rules, the exit and the settings in one package.
