### Care and reflection — 40 findings (11 critical, 21 high, 8 medium, 0 low)

_Monolith is a court, not a coach: it stamps immutable verdicts, offers no repair, no reflection and no weekly synthesis, while rivals like Opal, one sec and ScreenZen build repair channels, journaling and weekly reports into the product._

#### [CRITICAL] No repair or amnesty channel: a judged MISSED is immutable forever, with no appeal, partner override or streak-repair equivalent

Benchmark: Opal's own help page states its support team can check a broken streak 'and repair it, if applicable', and Opal ships Vacation Mode as a sanctioned pause state; ScreenZen lets an accountability partner unlock your settings and let you back in — mercy is a designed channel. Monolith: routineOutcome is declared immutable at birth — MonolithModels.kt:313-314 ('NULL until finalised by the one booking funnel, then ATTENDED / PARTIAL / MISSED / LATE_FIRE. Stamps are immutable.') — and the funnel refuses to revisit a stamped row (MonolithRepository.kt:1004 'if (session.routineOutcome != null) return session.routineOutcome'). There is no appeal, amend, partner-override or repair path anywhere in the codebase; the only forgiveness currency is one emergency token per week (MonolithWeek.kt emergencyBreaksRemainingFromSpendCount = 1 - spends) that must be spent before the failure, never after it. A MISSED stamped because of a funeral, a dead battery or the app's own shield gap is permanent and unanswerable.

Benchmark: one sec ships Journaling ('write down your thoughts and feelings to reflect and stay grounded'), Emotion Tracking and conversational-reflection interventions as headline features (one-sec.app / press kit); ScreenZen lets you type a reason for opening an app and earn opens by journaling in its Practice mode. Monolith: the session entity (MonolithModels.kt:268-370) contains only machine telemetry — HMAC signature, evidenceMask, shield heartbeat stamps, tamper flags — and not one user-authored reflection, note or mood field; the only self-report in the entire app is DayWordStore.kt:54's closed list WORDS = [REST, ILL, FAMILY]. The post-session ReceiptSheet is a display-only ledger whose footer (ReceiptSheet.kt) reads 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG' — literally: after a broken session the user is asked nothing, can record nothing, and learns nothing; the failure is filed for the machine, not processed by the person.

### Behaviour science — 40 findings (15 critical, 23 high, 2 medium, 0 low)

_Monolith implements blocking without implementation intentions: it records a goal and a clock, but never lets the user pre-decide 'if this cue, then this response', replay that decision at the intercept, or learn from whether it worked — the single best-evidenced behaviour-change technique in its category is entirely absent._

#### [CRITICAL] No if-then plan can be authored: 'intention' is a lone goal string, never a cue linked to a response

Science benchmark: Gollwitzer & Sheeran (2006) meta-analysis of 94 tests found if-then plans have a medium-to-large effect (d≈0.65) precisely because a goal is split into cue + pre-decided response; rivals approximate this visibly — one sec forces an intention/purpose picker before a target app opens, Opal makes the user 'set a timer and write an intention before using distracting apps'. Monolith has no such split anywhere: FocusSessionEntity carries only a single free-text intention:String (a goal, e.g. the fabricated default 'Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set' in MonolithViewModel.kt:226), and no entity in MonolithModels.kt has cue, response, obstacle or backup-plan fields — a user cannot author 'If I reach for Instagram when stuck, then I will do X' at all.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:267-270; app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/MonolithViewModel.kt:226`

#### [CRITICAL] No always-on friction: the pause exists only inside a pre-armed hard session, so habitual session-less opening — the exact behaviour the science targets — gets nothing

Benchmark: one sec and ScreenZen intercept every opening of a configured app, session or no session — the PNAS field study (Grüning et al., Max Planck/Heidelberg) measured exactly that habitual, unplanned opening and found 57% fewer openings over 6 weeks. Monolith: the accessibility interceptor bails before doing anything unless a focus session is already armed — MonolithAccessibilityService.kt:194-195 `val activeSession = dao.getActiveSessionSnapshot() ?: return@launch; if (!activeSession.isActive) return@launch`. Outside a manually started session — evenings, weekends, the 27 autopilot unlocks a day — Monolith applies zero friction to any app, so the single behaviour with published evidence behind it is the one behaviour it never touches.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/service/MonolithAccessibilityService.kt:194-195`

#### [CRITICAL] The habit loop only exists inside a sealed session — outside one, cue→craving→response runs completely untouched

one sec and ScreenZen are always-on: the breathing/escalating pause fires on every opening of a flagged app, all day, session or not (one sec PNAS field study: 57% fewer openings). Monolith's intervention exists only inside a sealed session: MonolithAccessibilityService returns immediately when there is no active session, so outside a session the cue (boredom, a notification, muscle memory) leads to the craved app with zero friction. The user must first win the hardest response in the loop — manually arming a session — before any craving is ever interrupted, which inverts the science: protection is conditional on the behaviour it is meant to create.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/service/MonolithAccessibilityService.kt:194-195`

#### [CRITICAL] Nothing at stake is ever shown at the moment of temptation: no at-risk streak, no end-of-day warning, no widget

Benchmark: ScreenZen puts the streak on the pause/intercept screen itself — App Store listing feature 10 'Streaks to encourage you not to exceed your limits or override your settings', and reviews confirm the streak is shown alongside the pause so 'seeing 12 consecutive days made me less likely to blow past the pause'; Opal 4.17 added 'Tap your streak to see where it stands and what it takes to keep it' plus home/lock-screen widgets. Loss aversion only works if the loss is salient at the decision moment; Monolith makes it salient nowhere.

### Delight and reward — 40 findings (10 critical, 20 high, 10 medium, 0 low)

_Monolith punishes and records like a machine but pays back almost nothing emotionally: no celebration moment, no spendable or chosen reward, no milestones, and its one crafted fanfare fires at the start of a session instead of the finish — the exact inverse of Forest, Opal and Duolingo-grade reward craft._

#### [CRITICAL] Session completion has no celebration moment at all — the finish is a static paper slip and the one reward it mints is never announced

Opal turns earning a gem into an interactive reveal — 'tap to crack it open, or skip straight to the shine' (App Store listing) — and Forest adds the grown tree to a visible forest plus coins at completion. Monolith's only completion surface is engineered to be the opposite: ReceiptSheet.kt:38-52 documents the slip as 'settled and still: it never re-strikes, never animates its numbers', entering with a plain fadeIn and dismissing on the next DOWN anywhere (ReceiptSheet.kt:60-77). Worse, the one reward the finish does mint is silent: MonolithRepository.kt:2049-2052 forges a curio ID inside the ending DB write with no announcement on the slip or anywhere at finish — the user only learns a session paid out if they later happen to open the Drawer cabinet.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:38-77; app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithRepository.kt:2049-2052`

#### [CRITICAL] All-or-nothing terminal schedule: no proportional or partial reward, and routine sessions can never earn at all

Forest pays proportionally and continuously: the tree grows throughout the session and completed sessions earn spendable coins scaled to success. Duolingo pays XP immediately per short lesson, so effort is never unrewarded. Monolith pays nothing until the very last block of the very last span: MonolithRepository.kt:2043-2051 sets forgedId only when allBlocksCompleted && !isRoutineSession, so a user who focuses 90% of a multi-block session, or who does all their focusing inside routines (finaliseRoutineSession at MonolithRepository.kt:1040 only preserves an existing forgedArtifactId, never mints one), earns exactly zero — the same payoff as never starting.

Monolith mints the artifact inside a repository tick (MonolithRepository.kt:2049-2050) and tells the user nothing: ReceiptState.kt contains no forged/artifact field at all (grep returns zero hits) and ReceiptSheet.kt renders only times, HELD counts and deflections, with its own header at ReceiptSheet.kt:35-40 mandating the slip 'never animates its numbers'. The only way to discover a reward exists is to later wander into DrawerScreen.kt:326ff's Cabinet and notice a row flipped to FORGED — reinforcement delayed by hours or never perceived.

Opal ships date-gated gems — Earth Gem 'Unlocked on Earth Day', Easter Gem 'Unlocked during Easter', Holi Gem 'Unlocked during Holi', Love Gem on Valentine's Day, Ramadan/Passover gems, Spring Gem on 1st day of spring, Summer Gem at solstice, Winter Gem 'during Holidays' (opalapp.com gem list) — and Forest ships seasonal/limited-edition trees, an Event Store with 10th Anniversary trees, and a Play Store live event 'Focus with friends, earn a Watermelon Tree House: log 750 minutes in Plant Together sessions' with an event countdown. Diwali, Christmas, New Year and exam season forge the identical random toy as any Tuesday — no scarcity, no FOMO, no reason to open the app this week rather than next.

### Design craft — 40 findings (7 critical, 23 high, 10 medium, 0 low)

_Monolith has no reading order: on every surface the largest, first thing is a duration, a countdown or an abstraction, while the task, the app, the user's own rules and even the name of the place itself are demoted to 11-15sp print below it._

#### [CRITICAL] Deck reads duration-first, work-last: the timer is the hero and the task is a footnote

Forest makes the focus subject itself the hero — a growing tree the session protects — and Opal's refreshed Home puts Opal Score, today's Screen Time and top distractions side-by-side at the top. Monolith inverts this: the Deck opens with a 10sp 'TOTAL' eyebrow, a 72sp duration hero (DialClockTextStyle) and a 288dp rotary wheel, and only below that card does the actual work appear as 'NOW' + task title in one 15sp single-line row, truncated with ellipsis, with QUEUE as 11sp side print. Duration — the least decision-relevant fact — gets ~360dp and the largest type in the app; what the user is supposed to be doing gets body size and one line.

Location: `TactileDeckScreen.kt:608-720 (hero/wheel), 770-850 (NOW task row at 15sp/11sp)`

#### [CRITICAL] Shield has flat, backwards reading order: bulk presets and ledgers before the searchable app list

Digital Wellbeing sorts most-used apps to the top so the app to limit is immediately actionable, and Opal's current rule editor 'asks for things in the order you actually think about them, and shows the Apps you've picked'. Monolith's Shield reads in the opposite order to use: LOADOUT (a preset that bulk-rewrites every tier) first, then ROUTINES, then the YOUR RULES standing-orders slip (unbounded PEEK/SHUT lines), and only as Section 4 does ALL APPS with its 40dp search field appear, followed by the catalogue, with BLOCKED WEBSITES last. Every section header is the identical 11.5sp grey FullBleedSectionHeader, so bulk presets, schedules, the user's own rulings, the searchable catalogue and websites carry no difference in rank — finding and blocking one named app requires scrolling past every abstraction first.

Location: `ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:282 (LOADOUT), 302 (ROUTINES), 406-432 (YOUR RULES slip), 434-480 (ALL APPS/search as Section 4), 541 (BLOCKED WEBSITES); MonolithCustomComponents.kt:123-152 (all headers 11.5sp onSurfaceVariant)`

Type.kt claims 'six sizes only - 104/72/50/22/15/10' yet screens inline 10.5sp, 11.5sp, 12.5sp, 13sp and 17sp throughout (DrawerScreen.kt alone has 40 inline fontSize declarations).

#### [CRITICAL] No platform component kit adopted at all — every control is a hand-drawn Canvas View bridged into Compose

Benchmark: ScreenZen, Opal, AppBlock and Google Digital Wellbeing are all built on their platform's native component kit, so every button, switch and slider inherits pressed/disabled/focused/error states, ripple, TalkBack semantics and font-scaling behaviour for free. Monolith adopts none of it: across the entire codebase there are zero imports of Material3 Button, Switch, Slider, Chip, Checkbox, RadioButton or Icon — the only Material3 types used anywhere are MaterialTheme, Text, HorizontalDivider and Scaffold. Every control is instead a hand-drawn legacy Android View rooted at BlockitCanvasView (ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:60), a 2,416-line Canvas file, with the whole legacy toolkit bridged back into Compose through AndroidView interop spread across 8 files (MainActivity, all four screens, three component files). Two UI toolkits, one interop seam, and no component ever gets a platform state model: each control's states exist only to the extent someone remembered to paint them.

#### [CRITICAL] No presence on any Android system surface: no Quick Settings tile, no home-screen widget, no launcher shortcuts

Monolith: AndroidManifest.xml declares only MainActivity, three services and receivers — zero TileService, zero AppWidgetProvider, zero shortcuts.xml/meta-data anywhere in app/src/main (grep for TileService/AppWidget/shortcut returns nothing). #### [CRITICAL] Five overlapping exit mechanisms where rivals ship one — cut Peek, Safe Break, Grace and the token valve down to a single break and a single emergency exit

Benchmark: Opal ships exactly one escape — 'Take a Break', up to 15 minutes, with a live countdown before blocking resumes; Fella ships exactly one 5-minute emergency unlock per session. Monolith ships five differently-named, differently-priced ways out: the 2-minute Peek lease (MonolithRepository.kt:106 PEEK_DURATION_SECONDS=120, plus a 20-minute cooldown in MonolithModels.kt:25), the 10-minute Safe Break (MonolithRepository.kt:110), the weekly-token Emergency Break requiring a 60-second hold (MonolithRepository.kt:121, 2168 'WEEKLY EMERGENCY BREAK — THE TOKEN'), the Grace Cancel outcome (MonolithRepository.kt:2325 SessionOutcome.GRACE_CANCEL), and break-between-blocks inside a multi-block session (MonolithModels.kt:387). A senior designer cuts this to one break and one emergency exit; five verbs for leaving means the user must learn five rulebooks at the exact moment of craving.

### Intentionality — 40 findings (10 critical, 20 high, 10 medium, 0 low)

_Monolith's four screens have no one-job discipline — the Deck and Shield each do five jobs, Tasks is done twice, and progress, the job that keeps users coming back, is done by no screen at all._

#### [CRITICAL] Deck has no single job: launcher, task manager, stats board, inbox and utilities tray in one screen

Forest's home screen does one job — set a timer (10-120 min), plant, grow/die (Forest reviews, 2026) — and AppBlock likewise isolates one-off blocking in Quick Block. Monolith's Deck is simultaneously session launcher, task manager, stats board, notification inbox and utilities tray: TactileDeckScreen.kt:96-156 takes dial/preset, checklist, activeTask/queuedTasks, profiles, intentionText, totalFocusedMinutes/totalInterceptions, capturedNotificationsCount, onOpenAlwaysOnDeskClock, onOpenNotificationDigest, weeklyEmergencyTokensRemaining and the seal/warrant apparatus in one signature. Starting a session — the only job that matters at that moment — competes for attention and scroll with queue management, lifetime totals and a desk clock.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:96`

#### [CRITICAL] A 1,072-line rotary wheel replaces the preset row every rival uses to start in one tap

Opal ships a home-screen widget that starts a session in two taps on 15/25/45-minute presets and Forest uses a plain 10-120 minute timer pick; Monolith deliberately deleted its preset tiles — 'The preset tiles are gone: one value, one control — the wheel' (TactileDeckScreen.kt:569) — even though four finished presets still exist unused in data (MonolithModels.kt:61-72 StudyModePreset POMODORO_25_5/DEEP_50_10/EXAM_90). In their place a single duration choice costs a 1,072-line custom Canvas control (BlockitCoreViews.kt:371 RotaryWheelView, with loadInertia/coastTau physics, Schmitt triggers, mesh curves and dot-matrix digits) plus a bespoke easing file (MonolithCurves.kt, 109 lines). Every session, forever, the user must drag-spin and land a precise minute instead of tapping the duration they used yesterday; there are no preset chips, no recents, and no widget or shortcut in AndroidManifest.xml. The wheel is decoration performing the job of a segmented button, at maximum learning and maintenance cost.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:371; app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:569`

#### [CRITICAL] The entire core action loop runs on invented verbs (ARM, SEAL, CUE, FORGE, SETTLE) with no glossary anywhere

Benchmarks use verbs the user already owns: Forest says 'Pick a focus length… Start focusing / Plant' (forestapp.cc), Opal sells 'Focus Sessions', Freedom 'Start Session / Locked Mode', Google Digital Wellbeing 'Focus mode' — the first tap is self-explanatory. Monolith's core loop is a private verb chain that must be memorised before it can be used: slide to ARM, wait for PROVING/SEAL, tasks are CUEd, the hero cycles DEPARTURE/RECESSION/SETTLE/SETTLED (app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:1129-1133), a finished record is FORGED/NOT YET FORGED (app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/screens/DrawerScreen.kt:486-488), and exit is an EMERGENCY BREAK VALVE (60S HOLD). A repo-wide search finds no glossary, tooltip or 'what is X' explanation for any of these terms, so every session start, end and history lookup pays a translation tax that rivals charge zero for.

#### [CRITICAL] No feature exists to make a session a commitment to anyone: no accountability partner, shared session, human-held override or stake — every promise is private and self-policed

Focusmate's entire session exists to be witnessed: partners share goals at the start, report accomplishment at the end, and carry a public attendance score (support.focusmate.com Getting Started); Forest's Plant Together kills everyone's tree if one person leaves; even ScreenZen and AppBlock let an accountability partner / trusted person hold the settings unlock. Monolith has no second human in any role: FocusSessionEntity (app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:269-360) records intention, durations, evidenceMask and held counts but no partner, witness, stake or share field exists anywhere in app/src/main/java, and the sole exit valve, weekly token and ratchet are all administered by the same person they constrain — a commitment nobody else knows about costs nothing to abandon.

Delete every costume and every function survives byte-identical; the elaborate feedback (pitch-scaled detents, latch clunks) reports only that a widget moved, never whether the user is any closer to the work the session was armed for.

### Together, live — 41 findings (16 critical, 20 high, 5 medium, 0 low)

_Monolith is architecturally incapable of live togetherness — no network permission, no identity, no other human can ever witness, join, or be failed by a session — while Forest, YPT and Focusmate prove live co-presence is the category's strongest retention and accountability mechanic._

#### [CRITICAL] No live co-focus room exists — no synchronized shared session of any kind

Forest ships Plant Together: create a room, invite friends by code, everyone (iOS and Android) plants the same tree in a synchronized session. Monolith has no room, join code, invite, or shared session state anywhere: its Room schema (app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:100-794) contains only single-device entities (tasks, blocked apps, sessions, routines, day notes) with no user, member, or room entity, and the four rail stops are DECK/SHIELD/TASKS/LEDGER (app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/views/MonolithRailView.kt:34) — there is no surface a second person could ever appear on.

#### [CRITICAL] The absence is architectural, not a missing screen: no INTERNET permission and every network/auth dependency is commented out

Forest rooms and YPT groups require a live backend; Monolith cannot reach one. AndroidManifest.xml declares no android.permission.INTERNET at all, and app/build.gradle.kts leaves the entire network stack disabled — firebase-firestore (line 107), firebase-auth (line 111), credentials/Google ID (lines 112-114) and retrofit (line 123) are all commented out. This is codified as a virtue in the UI itself: ParkDrawer.kt:121 prints 'DATA: ON THIS PHONE ONLY'. Adding co-focus is therefore not a feature task but a platform reversal: identity, sync, presence transport and moderation all have to be built from zero.

Benchmark: Play's crash-free bar is explicit — user-perceived crash rate must stay under 1.09% overall / 8% per device model or Play suppresses discoverability, and Crashlytics-guided teams target 99.5%+ crash-free users by detecting repeat exits via ApplicationExitInfo and degrading gracefully. A corrupt prefs/DB row that crashes on launch therefore crash-loops forever — the user's only fix is clear-data, which wipes every rule, routine and history record with it.

### Interaction detail — 40 findings (6 critical, 21 high, 12 medium, 1 low)

_Monolith's Canvas heroes are physically modelled down to hand-drawn contact shadows, but the Compose surface users actually tap has had press feedback deliberately deleted and never replaced — no ripple, no pressed state, no elevation and no compression — leaving it feeling dead and flat next to Opal, Material 3 rivals and even the platform defaults._

#### [CRITICAL] Pressing almost every button gives no visual answer at all — ripple is purged globally and no pressed state replaces it

Benchmark: Google Material 3 — shipped by Google Digital Wellbeing/Focus mode and inherited by native Android rivals such as AppBlock and ScreenZen — specifies an instant pressed state layer (10-12% opacity) plus ripple on DOWN, so the finger is acknowledged before the action fires. Monolith deletes it app-wide: Theme.kt:89-122 defines NoRippleIndication ('draws nothing for any interaction') and installs it via LocalIndication, with the comment that controls answer 'never a wash'; there is not one Material3 Button, collectIsPressed or isPressed in the codebase, and the universal CTA BlockitActionChip (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:170-215) is a flat Box with .clickable(onClick) and no interactionSource, scale, fill or elevation change. All 53 Compose .clickable sites therefore look identical finger-down and finger-off until the UP fires. The sole exception proves the omission is a choice, not a constraint: PARK's FIX key alone dips 1dp on press (ParkDrawer.kt:429).

Location: `Theme.kt:89-122; MonolithCustomComponents.kt:170-215`

#### [CRITICAL] The haptic language has no word for 'no': no error, warning or denial pattern exists, and refusals are voiced as successes

Apple's UINotificationFeedbackGenerator ships three semantically distinct, eyes-free-distinguishable patterns — success, warning and error (error = triple tap with rising intensity) — because outcome is the core haptic word. Monolith's entire named vocabulary in TactileSoundEngine.kt:625-860 is affirmative or neutral: playRotaryDetent, playFirmClick, playSeatKnock, playMechanicalLatch, playHarmonicSeal, playSealThrow, playTearPulse, playCompletionPulse — no error, warning, denied or rejected pattern exists anywhere in the engine. Refusals therefore borrow success voices: an arm-proving JAM — the app saying 'this seal failed' — is voiced in MonolithViewModel.kt:700-707 as three playSeatKnock(20, 1.0f, 320f) strikes, the same full-amplitude weighted knock used for successful seatings (MonolithViewModel.kt:1248). By feel alone a user cannot tell 'no' from 'done' — in an app whose whole product is 'no'.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/service/TactileSoundEngine.kt:625-860; app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/MonolithViewModel.kt:700-707`

Forest ships a library of Ambient Sounds (rain, cafe, meadow) the user layers over a focus session, plus Mindful Space soundscapes between sessions; Freedom ships Focus Sounds in-app for free — coffee-shop, office, library, nature recordings and composed focus music under a dedicated Sounds tab; Apple Background Sounds loops rain/ocean/noise for focus and can be tied to a Focus mode. A 25-minute or 4-hour session is sonically silent between its opening and closing clicks, so a user in a noisy cafe or open office must leave for Spotify/YouTube — apps Monolith itself may be blocking — to get the masking sound every serious rival provides in-house.

#### [CRITICAL] Entire Compose motion layer is fixed-duration tweens — no springs, no velocity, a generation behind the platform standard

Benchmark: Material 3 Expressive (shipped with Android 16, on Pixel from Sep 2025) replaced duration+easing pairs with physics-based springs as the primary motion model — springs carry velocity through interruption and settle by distance, so a reversed gesture never loses momentum. Monolith: zero spring() calls anywhere in the Compose layer (grep across app/src/main/java returns none); MonolithCurves.kt:66-73 offers only three TweenSpec factories, and every animated state — ParkDrawer fraction (ParkDrawer.kt:154-156), ShieldCapSelector cap travel (ShieldCapSelector.kt:85-87, fixed specA(260) whether the cap moves one stop or three), tab content, proof-strip alpha — is a fixed-duration tween that restarts with a velocity discontinuity when the user reverses mid-flight. #### [HIGH] One raw waveform for every motor on earth: no Composition primitives, no amplitude-capability check, no per-device tiering

Android provides VibrationEffect.Composition primitives (PRIMITIVE_CLICK, PRIMITIVE_THUD, PRIMITIVE_SPIN, PRIMITIVE_QUICK_RISE, PRIMITIVE_LOW_TICK) precisely so OEMs tune each effect to their own actuator's resonant frequency, with Vibrator.arePrimitivesSupported() as the documented capability check. Monolith calls none of it: grep across app/src/main finds zero uses of startComposition, createPredefined, arePrimitivesSupported or hasAmplitudeControl. Every pattern is a raw createWaveform of hand-picked millisecond/amplitude pairs (TactileSoundEngine.kt:551-572) authored as if every motor were identical, and the legacy path triggerOneShotHaptic (lines 575-601) quantises everything to just four durations (1/4/8/10ms) at DEFAULT_AMPLITUDE. Result: on cheap ERM phones the carefully enveloped latch/seal patterns collapse into indistinguishable buzz lengths, and on flagship Pixel/Samsung LRAs the app never touches the OEM-tuned primitives that make rivals feel crisp instead of generic.

#### [HIGH] No mixing exists: one serial mono queue that purges instead of blending, with no media-coexistence layer

Apple Background Sounds is a real mixer: a separate Volume slider, a separate 'Volume with Media' slider, 'Use When Media Is Playing' so the layer mixes under the user's music instead of fighting it, plus equalizer and left/right balance (Apple Support, Background Sounds). Forest likewise layers its ambient track over the session rather than replacing other audio. Monolith cannot layer anything: one LinkedBlockingQueue<SynthCommand>(64) feeds a single synth thread that polls, renders and writes one command to completion before touching the next (runFloatPcmSynthLoop, TactileSoundEngine.kt), both AudioTracks are CHANNEL_OUT_MONO (TactileSoundEngine.kt:397 and :434), every voice uses the same USAGE_ASSISTANCE_SONIFICATION attributes, and the seal 'mix' is actually a purge — playSealThrow clears the queue and pause+flushes the legacy track (TactileSoundEngine.kt:767+). Two sounds can never blend, ring under, or duck beneath anything; overlapping cues serialise, delay, or are discarded, and there is no bus on which a UI layer could ever sit at a different level from an alert layer.

#### [HIGH] Tween-only motion: not a single spring in the Compose layer, so no animation is interruptible or velocity-aware

Benchmark: Google's Material 3 Expressive (announced I/O May 2025, shipping in Android 16) replaced duration+easing pairs with physics-based springs (stiffness/damping) as the primary motion model precisely because springs carry velocity and can be interrupted and retargeted mid-flight; Apple's platforms have been spring-first for a decade. Monolith's Compose layer contains zero spring()/SpringSpec usages in the entire codebase. MonolithCurves.kt:12-32 freezes motion into a closed vocabulary of eight fixed durations (110-520ms) and three cubic-bezier curves, and everything — drawer (ParkDrawer.kt:154-156 animateTo with tween/EasingSeat), cap travel (ShieldCapSelector.kt:85 animateDpAsState), tab slides (MainActivity.kt:449-462) — is a fire-and-forget tween: interrupt or reverse one and it restarts its curve from zero velocity instead of continuing with the finger's momentum. The team hand-rolled viscous coast/capture physics for the Canvas wheel (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1249-1274), so the knowledge exists — it just never reached the Compose surfaces users touch most.

#### [MEDIUM] Off-cap grabs are silently unwinnable: the whole track accepts the touch, but a grab in the right half can never reach the catch before the finger runs out of screen

Monolith picks neither. beginAttempt (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1889-1915) starts a DRAG from a DOWN anywhere on the track, computes downOnCap but uses it only to classify taps, and sets grabOffsetPx = event.x - capCenter, so fingerFraction forever measures travel relative to the grab point. The view still consumes the gesture, calls requestDisallowInterceptTouchEvent(true), and fires the press-start feel (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1889-1925): the user gets a live, responsive-feeling drag that was doomed at DOWN, with no snap-to-touch, no magnetic attraction to the cap, and no rejection cue.

#### [MEDIUM] The gesture tracks a finger it never identifies: no active-pointer id, no POINTER_UP handling, no batched MOVE samples

Benchmark: Android's own MotionEvent contract (developer.android.com MotionEvent reference) states pointer order within an event can change between events and directs developers to track getPointerId/findPointerIndex, and to consume getHistoricalX samples because ACTION_MOVE batches multiple movements into one event. Monolith's SlideToStartView reads event.x — always pointer index 0 — in beginAttempt, dragMove, retreatMove and endDrag (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1889-2125), stores no pointer id, and has no ACTION_POINTER_UP branch at all (onTouchEvent, BlockitCoreViews.kt:1843-1887: POINTER_DOWN exists only as the mesh-abort trigger). A palm/second-finger contact, or the dragging finger lifting while another rests on the track, silently rebinds every coordinate to a different finger against the stale grabOffset — the cap teleports or the release is judged on the wrong finger. The same file's RotaryWheelView bothers to obtain and recycle a VelocityTracker (BlockitCoreViews.kt:496, 1049-1121); the flagship slide never does, and it also drops every historical sample in a batched MOVE, so fast flicks are reconstructed from the latest point only.

#### [LOW] Detent haptics are raw fixed waveforms — no OEM-tuned primitives, no capability check

Best-in-class Android pickers use VibrationEffect.Composition primitives (PRIMITIVE_TICK/PRIMITIVE_CLICK), which OEMs tune per actuator, gated by arePrimitivesSupported() — the platform answer to actuator fragmentation; iOS pickers likewise use the tuned UISelectionFeedbackGenerator. Monolith uses neither anywhere in the codebase (zero startComposition/PRIMITIVE_*/arePrimitivesSupported hits): the detent is one raw fixed waveform (7ms@180, 5ms@70) in TactileSoundEngine.playRotaryDetent, and the no-engine fallback is a createOneShot at DEFAULT_AMPLITUDE. The dial's signature tick is therefore a hardware lottery — crisp on one phone, sub-perceptual mush or a harsh buzz on another — with no capability query to adapt it.

### Comparative audit — 85 findings (24 critical, 43 high, 18 medium, 0 low)

_On a feature matrix Monolith is a single-device, single-mechanism blocker — three app tiers and a hand-typed domain list on one Android phone, with no keyword/category web rules, no network layer, no other platform, no context triggers and no session-free friction — while every serious rival ships several of those axes as table stakes._

#### [CRITICAL] Website blocking has exactly one rule type — a hand-typed exact domain; no keyword rules, no category filters, no adult-content database, no wildcards

AppBlock ships keyword blocking (block any URL containing a word, in-domain or anywhere in URL), adult-content blocking powered by a large database of 18+ URLs, and suggested-site lists; Cold Turkey ships wildcard URL patterns, keyword search blocking, importable pre-made web categories (e.g. Porn), per-URL/subreddit rules and YouTube-channel blocking; Freedom ships curated category filters (Social, News, Shopping, Gambling). Monolith's entire web rule model is one entity with a single string field: BlockedSiteEntity(domain) at app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:543-546, seeded with exactly 8 hand-typed domains (instagram.com, tiktok.com, reddit.com, x.com, twitter.com, facebook.com, snapchat.com, youtube.com/shorts) at MonolithModels.kt:507-517. There is no keyword rule type, no category filter, no curated list, no wildcard and no adult-content database anywhere in the codebase — a user who wants gambling or adult sites gone must enumerate the internet one domain at a time.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:507-546`

#### [CRITICAL] No blocking surface exists off this one Android phone — no desktop app, no browser extension, no iOS client, not even an INTERNET permission

Freedom runs on macOS, Windows, iOS, Android, ChromeOS and Linux (via Chrome) with sessions syncing across all of them — blocking Instagram on the phone blocks it on the laptop; Opal covers iOS, iPadOS, macOS and Android; ScreenZen covers iOS, Android, Mac and Windows; one sec adds Chrome/Firefox/Safari/Edge extensions. Monolith is a single-module Android project (settings.gradle.kts includes only ':app'; app/build.gradle.kts is one Android application, minSdk 24) whose AndroidManifest.xml does not even declare the INTERNET permission — the app is architecturally incapable of syncing a blocklist, an account, or a session to anything. Every distraction that lives on a laptop, desktop browser, tablet or iPhone is outside its universe by construction, so the moment the phone goes face-down the block ends.

Location: `settings.gradle.kts (include ':app' only); app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (no INTERNET permission declared)`

#### [CRITICAL] Routines have exactly one trigger — clock time — while rivals fire on location, Wi-Fi, usage and launch count

AppBlock's official Android help (appblock.app/help/android) gives every schedule five blocking conditions — Time, Location, Wi-Fi, Usage limit, Launch count — so rules fire on arriving at the office or joining home Wi-Fi. Monolith's RoutineEntity (MonolithModels.kt:550-570) carries exactly three scheduling fields — startMinutes, endMinutes, daysMask — plus pausedUntilMillis; there is no trigger-type field, no geofence/Wi-Fi/usage/launch input anywhere in RoutineDerive.kt or RoutineScheduler.kt, and AndroidManifest.xml:6-12 does not even declare a location permission. A Monolith routine can only ever know what o'clock it is, never where the user is or what they have already used.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:550-570`

#### [CRITICAL] No focus score, weekly report or trend verdict — statistics are banned by design, not just missing

Opal ships Focus Score (real-time focus level from distracting-app use, with history) plus a weekly Focus Report showing how screen time evolved, and AppBlock Insights adds a long-term Trend section. Monolith has no score, no periodic report and no period-over-period comparison anywhere: its only aggregate model is DailyFocusStat with three raw fields (MonolithModels.kt:473-479), computed by a hard-coded 7-day loop in MonolithRepository.kt:2361-2405, and the history surface's own charter forbids the rest — DrawerScreen.kt:57-65: 'It is not a dashboard, report card or attendance book: no totals, no streaks, no percentages, no counts.' A user gets no verdict on whether they are improving, which is the core retention loop of every analytics-led rival.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/screens/DrawerScreen.kt:57-65; app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:473-479; app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithRepository.kt:2361-2405`

#### [CRITICAL] No progression system at all: no levels, XP, achievements or streaks — history screen explicitly bans them

Opal ships a named achievement ladder of 20+ Gems tied to cumulative milestones (Driven Gem at 10 focus hours, Diligent at 100h, Dutiful at 500h, Devoted at 1,000h, plus day-streak gems at 2/5/10 days and seasonal gems), and even free ScreenZen puts streaks in its Progress tab. Monolith has no achievement, level, XP or streak entity anywhere: grep for xp/level/badge/achievement across the codebase returns nothing in the data layer, and the history screen is designed against progression — DrawerScreen.kt:58-62 declares the Drawer is 'not a dashboard, report card or attendance book: no totals, no streaks, no percentages, no counts'. The one streak visual that exists, TowerStreakView (BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:24, hardcoded default of 19 bricks at line 26), is never instantiated — its only other reference is a stray import at AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:62. A user can focus for a year and the app will show them exactly nothing more than on day one.

#### [CRITICAL] No study groups or co-focus rooms at all — the category's core retention loop is absent

YPT (Play listing, 5M users) ships study groups with group chat, friends' live study status and realtime category ranking, and app-blocking during sessions; Forest ships Plant Together rooms (create/join a room, synced sessions, if anyone leaves everyone's tree withers) free. Monolith has no group, room, friend or member concept anywhere: the 10 Room entities in MonolithModels.kt:100-794 are tasks, blocked apps, profiles, sessions, emergency spends, intercepts, notifications, sites, routines, guard settings and day notes — no social entity — and AndroidManifest.xml declares no INTERNET permission at all, so no group feature could function even if UI existed; Firebase Auth/Firestore that would power it are commented out in app/build.gradle.kts.

#### [CRITICAL] No accountability partner: every exit is self-approved, unlike AppBlock/ScreenZen partner-gated unlocks

AppBlock's Approval Access (appblock.app) lets a user assign a partner's email: turning Strict Mode off sends that partner a request they approve or deny, so the user cannot unilaterally quit; ScreenZen likewise offers an accountability partner who must unlock settings changes. Monolith's every escape is self-granted: the weekly emergency break is a self-held 60s valve recorded only as a local EmergencyBreakSpendEntity (MonolithModels.kt:442-443), peeks are self-tapped, and routines are self-edited — there is no contact, approver, or external-party field in any entity or screen, so the commitment device collapses to willpower, exactly the failure these rivals monetise against.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithModels.kt:442-443`

#### [CRITICAL] First run computes the user's real usage — then hides it: no baseline mirror moment at all

StayFree opens on a dashboard of the user's own real usage stats and Digital Wellbeing's first screen is the user's day chart; Opal computes a personal screen-time/savings figure inside onboarding. Monolith already fetches exactly this data on first launch — queryRealTodayUsageMinutes() (app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithRepository.kt:531) — but its only consumer is the silent catalogue reconcile at MonolithRepository.kt:247, feeding tier guesses. No first-run surface ever shows the user their own screen time, heaviest apps, or unlock counts: the one moment every rival uses to create motivation is computed by Monolith and thrown away.

Location: `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/MonolithRepository.kt:247,531`

AppBlock's Strict Mode offers 'Approval' as an access method alongside PIN, Charger and Timer, so a trusted person — not the tempted user — authorises changes; Opal likewise directs users to have a trusted person set the Screen Time passcode that locks its permission, so the grant cannot be self-revoked in a weak moment. Monolith's consent model is entirely self-administered on the same device: every grant in openFixPane (MainActivity.kt:363-410) is a Settings trip the session owner makes and can reverse alone, the device-admin receiver is self-enabled, and the emergency exit (DisarmChallengeOverlay, AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt) is a self-held 60-second valve — there is no approval request, partner code, account or delegated-consent code path anywhere in the app.

## Supplement: Blockit head-to-head (from its actual APK)

Evidence base: clean, unmodded Blockit v2.2.7 (com.hypenet.focused, versionCode 152) APK, signing certificate verified against the developer original, statically reverse-engineered only — never installed or run. Full evidence: blockit-re/EVIDENCE.md. Findings about store presence and monetisation were removed under the same rule as the main report; what remains is implementation contrast only the APK could prove.

### Blockit — Head-to-head losses — 19 findings (5 critical, 11 high, 3 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] The copy kept the 3-stop selector but not the 3 bags behind it: Monolith stores only one global tier set, so no per-context app set can exist

Blockit EVIDENCE §7.2/§7.5: bags are stored, named, switchable sets — layout ids bagSlot0..5/bagIcon0..5, pref keys active_bag and bag_name_<n>, 'routine 1 uses bag 1, routine 2 uses bag 2, routine 3 uses bag 3' (routine_bag_linked, bag_before_routine); Premium is literally '3 bags instead of 1'. Monolith has no bag/set entity at all: BlockedAppEntity carries exactly one global blockTier per package (MonolithModels.kt:231-247), SmartLoadout is three fixed developer-written enums — STUDY/WORK_SPRINT/SLEEP (MonolithModels.kt:38-65) — LoadoutStore persistently stores only the last hand-picked loadout's name (LoadoutStore.kt:35-44), and applySmartLoadout recomputes and overwrites every app's tier from categories/substrings (MonolithRepository.kt:1126-1171). Per-context membership is therefore impossible: Spotify cannot be OPEN in an evening set and LOCKED in a study set, because there is only ever one tier row to hold either fact, and the 3-stop selector selects a rewrite, not one of three preserved sets.

Recommendation: Add a real bag layer: a (bagId, packageName) membership / per-loadout tier-snapshot table for at least 3 named, user-editable bags, with the selector switching the active bag instead of rewriting global tiers; routines should reference a bag id, as Blockit's routine_bag_linked does.

#### [CRITICAL] Bankable 99-deep parachute stockpile vs an expiring 1-per-week mint that never accumulates

Blockit EVIDENCE §7.3: parachutes are held inventory — pref keys parachute_count/parachute_sig, cap string parachute_limit_toast='You can hold up to 99 parachutes', earned via first-one-free, Google sign-in welcome, and a 100-day streak gift, and bought (see §10). Monolith: MonolithWeek.kt:41-42 emergencyBreaksRemainingFromSpendCount is (1 - spendCount).coerceAtLeast(0) against the Monday-anchored current week only (MonolithWeek.kt weekAnchorMillis), and TactileDeckScreen.kt:1047-1048 prints the badge '$tokens/1 WEEK'. Unspent Monolith tokens do not roll over: a quiet week still leaves exactly 1, never 2. Priced concretely: two emergencies clustered in one week cost a Blockit user with a banked stock 2 of up to 99 parachutes; the same cluster costs a Monolith user the first exit plus an unbuyable wait until next Monday 00:00 — up to ~7 days — regardless of how many clean weeks preceded it.

Recommendation: Make the emergency balance bankable inventory rather than a weekly mint: persist a count, let unspent weeks accumulate up to a stated cap, and show the balance as a stock (e.g. '3 parachutes'), not 'x/1 WEEK'.

#### [CRITICAL] Blockit's tower forgives a missed day (reserve blocks, then a parachute repair); Monolith's has no repair state at all

Blockit EVIDENCE.md §7.4: tower_reserve_sheet_* — 'Every 10 days in a row you earn a reserve block (up to 3). If you miss a day, a reserve block repairs the tower on its own'; repair_* — when reserves are out, 'Only a parachute can repair the tower now' (repair_use_parachute/repair_buy_parachute), and §9 syncs the 'repaired' tower days to Firebase. Monolith has no reserve, repair or fall state anywhere: the only tower-adjacent persistence is a binary curio set — MonolithDao.kt:74 'SELECT DISTINCT forgedArtifactId FROM focus_sessions WHERE forgedArtifactId IS NOT NULL' and MonolithRepository.kt:671 forgedArtifactIds() returning Set<String>. No entity field stores reserves, repaired days or a broken streak.

Recommendation: Add a persisted streak record (current run, reserves earned/spent, repaired dates) with Blockit's two-tier forgiveness: auto-spend a reserve block earned every 10 consecutive days (cap 3) on a missed day, then offer the weekly emergency token as the paid repair when reserves are exhausted — instead of a miss being unrecoverable and unrecorded.

#### [CRITICAL] Blockit credits any day totalling 5 minutes; Monolith pays out only on a fully completed non-routine session

Blockit EVIDENCE.md §7.4 tower_info_*: 'Every day with at least five minutes of session lays a block. Seven blocks make a floor'; §8 scaffolds the very first session at 5 minutes to lay the first brick — daily aggregate minutes, not session completion, is the unit. Monolith inverts it: MonolithRepository.kt:2049-2050 forges a curio only 'if (allBlocksCompleted && !isRoutineSession)' — a random CurioCatalog pick — and its only daily aggregation, MonolithRepository.kt:2390, defines a block as '(totalMins / 25).coerceAtLeast(if (totalMins >= 15) 1 else 0)'. A 5-14 minute day, a partial session, and every routine session therefore build exactly nothing in Monolith.

Recommendation: Make the tower brick a daily-aggregate fact: one brick for any calendar day with >=5 verified session minutes, regardless of which session or routine produced them or whether a session ran to completion. Keep curios as a separate completion reward instead of letting them substitute for the daily brick.

#### [CRITICAL] A routine firing permanently destroys the user's hand-set app rules — Blockit swaps a saved Bag and restores it, Monolith rewrites every app row and never restores

Blockit (EVIDENCE.md §7.5, §7.2): each routine is bound to its own curated Bag (strings routine_bag_setting_* 'Routine 1 uses bag 1, routine 2 uses bag 2, routine 3 uses bag 3', pref routine_bag_linked) and pref bag_before_routine saves the pre-routine bag — firing is a non-destructive pointer swap. Monolith: RoutineEntity carries only a loadoutName string naming one of three fixed SmartLoadout presets (MonolithModels.kt:550-556); MonolithRepository.materialiseRoutineSession (MonolithRepository.kt:1086-1089) calls applySmartLoadout, which recomputes every app's tier from category/substring heuristics (MonolithRepository.kt:1126-1165) and persists the rewrite with dao.insertApps(updated). No snapshot or restore of the prior tiers exists anywhere (no equivalent of bag_before_routine).

Recommendation: Give each routine its own stored per-app tier set (its Bag), snapshot the live tiers on materialise, and restore them at window end — never let a scheduled session overwrite the user's manual rules with heuristic preset tiers.

#### [HIGH] Blockit has a working screen-off backup hand when accessibility dies; Monolith's device admin can never lock anything

Blockit EVIDENCE.md §6.3: res/xml/device_admin_uses_policies.xml declares exactly one policy, <force-lock/>, and LockManager j9/a holds a DevicePolicyManager and calls lockNow() (~line 384); strings accessibility_stuck_backup/backup_hand_*/backup_eyes_* describe the degraded mode honestly — if accessibility dies, opening anything turns the screen off, and the user is told even Bag apps will be blocked because the backup 'cannot tell one app from another'. Monolith instead declares <limit-password/> in app/src/main/res/xml/device_admin_receiver.xml:3-5, a policy no code exercises, and its whole admin implementation (app/src/main/java/com/example/service/MonolithDeviceAdminReceiver.kt, 28 lines) is an onDisableRequested warning string plus WatchStore grant stamps — grep finds no lockNow() anywhere, and MonolithRepository.kt:708 uses DevicePolicyManager only for isAdminActive(). So Monolith spent its one device-admin slot on a password policy it never uses and has no screen-off fallback at all: when its accessibility service dies mid-session, the sniper, site blocker and Settings guard (all accessibility-only branches in MonolithAccessibilityService.kt) simply stop enforcing, with nothing cruder-but-alive behind them.

Recommendation: Replace the unused limit-password policy with <force-lock/> and implement the degraded mode Blockit ships: when the accessibility binding is lost mid-session, call lockNow() on blocked-app foreground attempts via the shield door, and tell the user in plain language that per-app distinction is lost in backup mode.

#### [HIGH] Blockit detects with one event-driven door and uses UsageStats only as a permission probe; Monolith runs a second, divergent guess-detector in parallel

Blockit EVIDENCE.md §6.1-6.2: foreground detection is purely accessibility-event-driven (BlockAccessibilityService, config 0x00400020), and UsageStats is explicitly NOT the detector — utility class d7/f0 only calls queryUsageStats(INTERVAL_YEARLY, now-1_000_000ms, now) and returns !list.isEmpty() as a permission-granted probe; no queryEvents/MOVE_TO_FOREGROUND exists in first-party code. Monolith runs both systems at once as rival detectors: the accessibility service (MonolithAccessibilityService.kt) plus MonolithShieldService.kt:193 delay(2000L) polling MonolithRepository.queryForegroundBlockedApp (MonolithRepository.kt:564-580), which guesses the foreground app from INTERVAL_DAILY stats filtered to lastTimeUsed within 8s. The two doors do not even compute the same blocked set: the shield rebuilds its set with its own peek/safe-break filter at MonolithShieldService.kt:165-186, while the accessibility door applies separate sniper, site and lease branches — so the same app in the same second can be blocked by one door and passed by the other, and the 2s guess door can fire intercepts for an app the user already left.

Recommendation: Demote UsageStats in Monolith to what Blockit uses it for — a grant probe — and make the accessibility event the single foreground detector; keep the shield service as session timer/heartbeat only, so there is one blocked-set computation and one intercept path to keep consistent.

#### [HIGH] Blockit detects the 'service switched on but not running' stuck state and holds a guardian screen with a 1-minute re-enable grace; Monolith has no stuck-service recovery at all

Blockit EVIDENCE.md §6.4: strings accessibility_stuck_title/'The service is stuck' name the exact failure — 'The system keeps the lock service switched on but no longer runs it, so a session would not block anything' — with Open settings / Start anyway choices; the guardian_down_* family adds a mid-session recovery: blockit 'has to stay in front until the session ends', grants one minute to re-enable the service, and if the grace is exhausted the lock screen stays until the session ends, implemented via the transparent GuardianPassActivity trampoline (calls LockManager a.f(this).g() then finishes); its boot receiver also re-arms on USER_PRESENT/USER_UNLOCKED. Monolith has no equivalent anywhere: grep finds no USER_PRESENT/USER_UNLOCKED receiver, no guardian or stuck-service flow, and MonolithAccessibilityService.kt's liveness proof is only the in-memory instance/lastRootMono stamps in its companion object — measurements the arm-proving cascade reads before a session, not a recovery path offered to a user whose service was switched on but stopped running mid-session. The failure Blockit names and walks the user through is, in Monolith, silent loss of the accessibility doors until the user happens to notice.

Recommendation: Add Blockit's two-part recovery: detect the enabled-but-not-running accessibility state (grant string present, no live binding/root stamp) and surface its Open-settings/Start-anyway choice, plus a mid-session guardian state that holds the block screen in front with a timed re-enable grace instead of silently unenforcing.

#### [HIGH] No scarcity: Blockit hard-caps the Bag at 3 apps (6 paid), Monolith lets unlimited apps be OPEN or PEEK — a session can be sealed holding nothing

Blockit EVIDENCE §7.2: the Bag's power is its hard scarcity — 'YOUR BAG · 3 APPS FOR THE JOURNEY', free tier 1 bag/3 apps, and HomeActivity enforces the cap in code (slot cap = bag_six_owned ? 6 : 3, ~lines 3821/6244); the 6-slot expansion is a paid add-on (bag_six). Monolith imposes no cap in either direction of its tier system: any number of apps can be OPEN and any number PEEK_2M (AppBlockTier, MonolithModels.kt:13-36), countHeldApps only counts the non-OPEN set for the seal snapshot (MonolithRepository.kt:1316-1319) and startSession performs no minimum-held check, while peek leases and their 20-minute cooldowns are strictly per-package (BlockedAppEntity activePeekUntil/lastPeekEnd fields; MonolithRepository.kt startPeekLease ~L1199). A user can pre-excuse every distraction — all OPEN, or all PEEK and then rotate app-to-app, each with its own fresh 2 minutes — and still seal a 'focus' session that holds nothing.

Recommendation: Import the scarcity, not just the suitcase shape: cap OPEN+PEEK membership per loadout (e.g. a small fixed slot count with visible empty slots), refuse or loudly warn on arming a session whose held count is zero, and make the peek cooldown shared across PEEK apps rather than per-package so rotation cannot defeat the ration.

#### [HIGH] Blockit exempts phone/contacts/camera/clock from the Bag entirely; Monolith puts them in the tier economy with no always-allowed floor in enforcement

Blockit EVIDENCE §3/§6.8/§8: calls and core phone surfaces are outside the Bag economy entirely — manifest <queries> covers ACTION_DIAL, APP_CONTACTS, APP_MESSAGING, IMAGE_CAPTURE and SHOW_ALARMS, boarding_note_block states 'Calls always work, even during a block', and the tour says phone, messages and camera 'stay at your fingertips' whether or not they are packed. Monolith gives enforcement no such floor: MonolithShieldService.kt:166-177 builds the blocked set purely from resolvedTier (OPEN exempt, leased/safe-break PEEK exempt, everything else blocked) with no package-level exemption, and the dialler/camera/contacts are ordinary BlockedAppEntity rows whose fate a loadout decides — STUDY demotes all MESSAGING to a 2-minute PEEK (MonolithRepository.kt:1131-1134) and only SLEEP spares anything, by substring-matching 'dialer/phone/clock/alarm/maps' (MonolithRepository.kt:1152-1160), a list camera and contacts are not even on.

Recommendation: Add a non-tierable always-allowed floor in the shield/accessibility enforcement itself — dialler/in-call UI, contacts, camera, clock/alarms — that no loadout, profile or hand-set tier can revoke, matching Blockit's guarantee that these surfaces never consume a slot and never need one.

#### [HIGH] Parachute is a multi-job currency — exit, Tower repair, and a held key for >3h sessions, routines and +15 min extensions; Monolith's token gates and repairs nothing

Blockit EVIDENCE §7.1/§7.5/§7.4: one parachute unit does four jobs — (a) consumed to exit early (slide_exit_costs='Uses 1 parachute'), (b) consumed to repair the Tower after a missed day (repair_use_parachute='Use a parachute (%d)'), (c) held, not spent, as a gate: sessions over 3h require one aboard (parachute_required_long), routines require at least one aboard (parachute_required_routine), and the in-session +15 min extension requires one aboard (countdown_extend_need_parachute). Monolith's token has exactly one consumer chain: grep shows emergencyBreaksRemaining/weeklyEmergencyTokensRemaining read only by the Deck badge (TactileDeckScreen.kt:1048) and the Disarm overlay (MainActivity.kt:803), and the only spend write is completeEmergencyBreak() (MonolithRepository.kt:2225-2246). No routine start, session-length tier, extension, or streak/Tower repair anywhere reads or spends it. Monolith copied the scarcity (1/week, 60s hold at MonolithRepository.kt:121 EMERGENCY_BREAK_HELD_SECONDS=60, Emergency60sValveView requiredSeconds=60) but none of the utility that makes holding the original's unit valuable even when you never exit.

Recommendation: Give the token the original's other jobs or stop aping its scarcity: e.g. require one aboard (unspent) to arm routines or over-length sessions, allow +15 min extension with one aboard, and allow spending one retrospectively to repair a missed routine/streak day.

#### [HIGH] Blockit's parachute balance is signed and Firebase-synced as portable property; Monolith's ledger is unsigned, local-only spend rows that can never carry an economy

Blockit EVIDENCE §7.3/§9: the parachute count is treated as durable property — pref keys parachute_count + parachute_sig with log string 'getParachuteCount: signature mismatch, resetting', and Firebase Realtime Database sync in it.mirko.stats.h merging 'parachute server=%d local=%d -> max', so a signed-in user's earned/bought stock survives reinstall and device change and tampering with the local count is detected. Monolith: EmergencyBreakSpendEntity (MonolithModels.kt:442-449) is a plain unsigned local Room row (id, sessionId, spentAtWallMillis, weekAnchorMillis, heldSeconds) and the token is purely derived from those local rows (MonolithRepository.kt:2177-2179); there is no account, no sync, and no signature over the spend ledger anywhere. That forecloses the whole economy above: an unsigned, device-local, week-expiring ledger cannot carry earnable, purchasable or portable exits, because there is nothing trustworthy or transferable to sell, gift at a 100-day streak, or restore.

Recommendation: If exits are ever to be earned/bought/banked, rebuild the ledger as Blockit does: a signed count (signature over the balance, reset-on-mismatch) with account sync taking max(server, local), instead of unsigned local spend rows whose only possible policy is the current weekly re-mint.

#### [HIGH] Blockit actively saves the streak before the day is lost — evening reminder, danger banner and streak widget; Monolith never warns

Blockit EVIDENCE.md §7.4/§4.3/§7.7: StreakReminderReceiver (evening nudge, pref streak_reminder_enabled, 'if you haven't done at least five minutes of session today'), streak_danger_* banner family in _notification_danger.xml ('The day is ending', 'Five minutes of session save the tower', last-chance variant when reserves are gone), a dedicated streak notification channel (§6.9), and StreakWidgetProvider ('Your streak, the top of the tower', §7.7). Monolith has no streak reminder receiver, no danger banner and no widget provider anywhere in app/src/main/java, and its tower view (BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:24 TowerStreakView) is a passive canvas that is never even instantiated — only imported unused at AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:62.

Recommendation: Add the save-the-day loop: an evening check against today's verified minutes that fires a '5 minutes saves the tower' reminder only when the brick is not yet laid, escalates when no reserve block remains, and surfaces the current streak on a home-screen widget.

#### [HIGH] Blockit's tower is a permanent, backed-up monument (founded date, tallest-tower record, cloud-synced days); Monolith stores no tower history to keep

Blockit EVIDENCE.md §7.4: _activity_tower.xml is a dedicated screen (view it.mirko.widget.graph.LevelGraph) printing 'YOUR TOWER: %d DAYS', tower_founded 'Founded on %s', tower_record 'Personal record: %d days' and footer tower_foot_minutes/avg/best/record (TOTAL TIME, AVG MIN/DAY, BEST DAY, TALLEST TOWER); §7.6/§9 back it with per-day Room Records (date:String, time:int, timeList) synced to Firebase including repaired days, and streak_restart_* memorialises a fall ('The tower has fallen') while the record survives. Monolith has no founded date, no tallest/record field and no per-day tower table: MonolithModels.kt:799-807 CurioCatalog is a fixed list of 6 text artifacts and MonolithDao.kt:74 collapses all history to the DISTINCT set of forged ids, so there is no height, date or best run to display, export or restore after a reinstall.

Recommendation: Persist a per-day tower ledger (date, verified minutes, brick laid/reserve-repaired) as the source of truth, derive founded date, current height and tallest-ever from it, show those four footer stats on a dedicated tower screen, and include the ledger in backup/sync so the monument survives a device change.

#### [HIGH] No routine pre-alert: Blockit warns minutes before an auto-session locks the phone, Monolith's routine materialises in silence

Blockit (EVIDENCE.md §6.9, §7.5): a dedicated it.mirko.timer.RoutinePreAlertReceiver and a HIGH-importance (4) channel it.mirko.block.ROUTINE_PREALERT, text 'Your block session begins at %1$s, in %2$d minutes. Get ready.', backed by prefs auto_session_prealert / prealert_session_at — the warning is separate machinery from the AutoSessionReceiver that starts the session. Monolith: a codebase-wide search finds zero pre-alert code, strings, channel or preference; RoutineHeartbeat.kt:140-151 simply materialises the session when derive() says the window is open, and the first user-visible signal is the shield service's own foreground notification after the block has already started.

Recommendation: Add a pre-alert alarm/notification X minutes before each routine window (its own channel, time + routine name), scheduled from the same nextBoundary computation RoutineScheduler already performs, so a scheduled lock never ambushes the user mid-task.

#### [HIGH] Blockit warns about overlapping routines at setup and shows the merged lock; Monolith lets routines silently swallow each other

Blockit (EVIDENCE.md §7.5): strings routine_overlap_* — 'Routine %1$d and routine %2$d overlap: you'll be locked from %3$s to %4$s.' with a 'Turn on anyway' choice, computed when the user enables a routine. Monolith: the routine editor exposes only toggle/time/day/loadout callbacks (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:110-115, RoutineRow at :643) and no overlap check exists in the editor or persistRoutine path; overlap is discovered only inside RoutineDerive.deriveOne (RoutineDerive.kt:154-160), where the second routine is silently parked as OPEN_HELD (and its closed window judged HELD at :215) — it never fires and the user is never told a conflict exists or what the combined locked span is.

Recommendation: At edit/enable time, detect routine-vs-routine window overlap, show the merged locked interval as Blockit does, and require an explicit 'turn on anyway' confirmation; also surface HELD-swallowed windows in the routine row instead of burying them in derivation state.

#### [MEDIUM] Blockit explicitly classifies and avoids lockscreen/PIN/biometric windows; Monolith has no keyguard awareness and relies only on a blanket systemui package skip

Blockit EVIDENCE.md §6.1: BlockAccessibilityService (1,240 lines) imports KeyguardManager and InputMethodManager (enumerating IMEs) and carries a lockscreen classifier matching window text against 'keyguard|bouncer|lockscreen|pin|pattern|password|biometric|fingerprint|face|unlock|credential|puk|knox|secscreen' — built specifically to avoid fighting the lock screen, PIN/pattern entry, biometric prompts and OEM secure screens (Knox/secscreen are named). Monolith has zero such awareness: grep for keyguard/lockscreen/bouncer/isKeyguard across app/src/main/java returns no hits, and MonolithAccessibilityService.onAccessibilityEvent exempts only its own package and anything starting with com.android.systemui before running its DB-backed enforcement (settings-guard text walk, sniper, URL bar) on every other package. On skins where credential/bouncer windows live outside com.android.systemui's package, Monolith's only protection against intercepting an unlock surface is an accident of AOSP packaging; Blockit engineered the exemption explicitly, by content, across OEMs.

Recommendation: Port the classifier concept: before any enforcement branch, skip events whose window text/package indicate keyguard, bouncer, credential, biometric or IME surfaces (including OEM variants such as Knox), instead of relying solely on the com.android.systemui package prefix.

#### [MEDIUM] Where the copy out-built the original: Blockit Bag apps are unlimited for the whole session, Monolith's PEEK_2M rations them to 2 minutes plus a 20-minute cooldown

Blockit EVIDENCE §7.2/§6.8: a Bag app is simply usable — it 'stays at your fingertips' for the whole session, and no per-app time ration, lease or cooldown mechanism for bag apps appears anywhere in the APK evidence; packing WhatsApp or a reader means unlimited use of it until the session ends. Monolith's invented middle tier is stricter than the original: PEEK_2M is defined as a 2-minute check-in with a mandatory 20-minute cooldown (MonolithModels.kt:13-36), implemented as a 120-second lease (MonolithRepository.kt startPeekLease, PEEK_DURATION_MILLIS) with the cooldown anchored per package. That is a genuine improvement for semi-trusted apps (messaging, YouTube in STUDY) that Blockit's binary in/out model cannot express — a packed app in Blockit is an all-session hole, a PEEK app in Monolith is a ration.

Recommendation: Keep and advertise the middle tier rather than simplifying toward Blockit's binary model; consider offering it explicitly as the Monolith differentiator ('packed apps are rationed, not unlimited'), and do not let bag/set work regress PEEK apps to unlimited OPEN-style access within a session.

#### [MEDIUM] Simplicity gap: Blockit runs routines on six flat preference keys; Monolith built an ~800-line judgement engine that grades the user for the same start/end/days feature

Blockit (EVIDENCE.md §7.5): a routine is stored as SharedPreferences keys auto_session_enabled/days/hour/minute/minutes/prealert plus active_routine/routine_index/routine_name_<n>, fired by AutoSessionReceiver — no database entity, no outcome grading; the session either starts or it doesn't. Monolith implements the same user-visible feature as a Room RoutineEntity (MonolithModels.kt:550-571, including pausedUntilMillis and scheduleEditedAtMillis bookkeeping fields) plus RoutineSchedule window math (MonolithModels.kt:574-740), RoutineDerive.kt (290 lines: 8 WindowStates, 7 WindowJudgements including MISSED/PARTIAL/NOT_DELIVERED attendance verdicts stamped on sessions), RoutineHeartbeat.kt (189 lines), RoutineScheduler.kt and RoutineAlarmReceiver.kt — and Blockit ships no MISSED-style grading of routine attendance at all.

Recommendation: Treat Blockit's model as the baseline spec: a routine is enabled+days+start+duration+its bag+pre-alert. Strip or quarantine the judgement layer (WindowJudgement, edit-horizon, pause-amnesty semantics) behind a deliberate product decision, since none of it exists in the original and it is the surface most routine complexity and disputes come from.
